“Hollywood or nightmare”.
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
21:42:26 UTC
06:42:26 KST

Photos courtesy of Natalia Pershko. Art: Mediazona
In August, Mediazona broke the story of Oleg Varyukhin, the man charged with treason in Russia for paying mandatory taxes as a small business owner in Ukraine. Now, his estranged daughter, who fled the war to Europe, has come forward after accidentally discovering her father’s fate online, while a Moscow court extends his arrest citing his “clandestine skills”.
Ksenia was only four years old when her parents divorced. It happened only a few years after the family had moved from Arctic city of Norilsk to a small town in Ukraine’s Zhytomyr region; her father, Oleg Varyukhin stayed, while her mother took Ksenia and her older sister to another region. They had not spoken since.
But one evening this summer, her husband, Ravil Ganeev, was scrolling through Instagram when he stumbled upon a Mediazona post about a 61-year-old businessman who had been arrested at a Moscow airport and charged with treason.
“Isn’t this your father?” he asked his wife.
Ksenia recognised him immediately. “Even though we haven’t communicated for a long time, since my parents divorced when I was a child, this news was a crushing blow,” the 21-year-old told Mediazona.
Oleg Varyukhin’s arrest is among a series of shocks to Ksenia and her husband. After the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Ksenia fled to Sweden under a temporary protection programme. Online, she met Ganeev, a Russian citizen who had fled his own country due to his anti-war views; Russian authorities have placed him on a wanted list for the “justification of terrorism” which he links to his social media posts against the war. In 2024, they married.
When Swedish authorities denied Ganeev asylum claim (despite a criminal case in Russia), Ksenia refused to leave her husband, and the couple was forced to relocate again. Recently, with the help of human rights defenders, France granted Ganeev a humanitarian visa.
“And now, when my father was also detained, I feel like the circle of persecution has closed around my entire family,” Ksenia says. “I have this feeling that this is just some kind of Hollywood film or total nightmare.”
Mediazona first reported on Varyukhin’s case in August. The 61-year-old former pilot, who ran a small perfume shop in Ukraine for decades, travelled to Moscow this May to sort out expired paperwork—born in the USSR, he even left the country for the last time using his Soviet passport. FSB officers at Vnukovo airport searched his phone and found tax receipts. Because Varyukhin was legally obligated as a businessman to pay Ukraine’s mandatory military tax, introduced in 2014 to support the armed forces, the Russian state charged him with treason for “financing” the enemy.
Despite the absurdity of equating tax compliance with treason, the Russian justice system continues to process his case. On September 17, Moscow’s Meshchansky Court extended Varyukhin’s pre-trial arrest until December 21. In its ruling, the court noted that the accused is “prone to constantly changing his place of residence” and “possesses clandestine skills.”
The court also formally declared Varyukhin a Russian citizen. His lawyer, Yuri Shel, continues to object that his client cannot be a subject of Article 275 of the Criminal Code (“Treason”) because he never even received a Russian passport, having left for Ukraine in the late nineties on his old Soviet documents. The court, however, relies on a 1991 law that automatically granted citizenship to former Soviet citizens who were permanently residing in Russia on February 6, 1992—when Varyukhin was living in the Arctic city of Norilsk.
During pre-trial detention, Varyukhin remains upbeat. “He stays positive. He asks for work, offering to voluntarily wash the dirty walls of the exercise yard with soap to clean off the spit and grime. They refused him,” Shel says. “He says: I can’t sit idle, I want to be of use to people.”
Varyukhin’s current wife, Natalia Pershko, who waited for him at the Moscow airport while he was being subjected to the first of several “carousel” arrests, is preparing to bring him warm clothes. Beyond occasional letters she has no news of her husband.
Natalia is also from Siberia and had also moved to the Zhytomyr region in the 1990s; they were raising a son, Georgy. She says Varyukhin attempted to obtain Ukrainian citizenship multiple times but was rejected, despite having Ukrainian-born kids, properties, and running a perfume business. The couple lived quietly on their old documents, running their shop and caring for stray cats until the full-scale invasion shattered their familiar life. In 2024, Ukrainian migration officials unexpectedly refused to renew Natalia’s residence permit—which she had held for nearly a quarter of a century—and gave her two weeks to leave the country.
She eventually settled with their son in neighbouring Moldova. Varyukhin sold his car to fund their relocation but stayed behind in Ukraine to keep their shop afloat, which was their only source of income. Fearing he would be barred from re-entering Ukraine if he left, the couple lived apart for nearly two years.
It wasn’t until the spring of 2026 that Varyukhin finally travelled to Chișinău to reunite with his family. From there, armed with a temporary return certificate issued by the consulate on his old Soviet passport, the couple boarded a flight to Moscow to finally update his documents. He was detained upon arrival.

OA-1K Goes Off Runway at Oklahoma Airport; Crew Safe
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
21:41:23 UTC
06:41:23 KST

An OA-1K Skyraider II belonging to Air Force Special Operations Command went off the runway while landing at a small Oklahoma City airport Oct. 5 and is waiting to be moved, according to officials and flight tracking data.
Local media outlets first reported on the incident, which occurred at Sundance Airport about 20 miles from Will Rogers Air National Guard Base where the plane took off.
The two crew members on board are safe, a spokesperson for the 492nd Special Operations Wing confirmed to Air & Space Forces Magazine.
The incident occurred during a training sortie just a few days after the 492nd announced on social media that the OA-1K’s formal training unit had started training its first class of new pilots. The wing spokesperson declined to say whether one of the new student pilots was on board during the incident.
The OA-1K is a “combat scout” adapted from a cropduster that Air Force special operators plan to use for light attack and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions in less contested airspace, particularly for counterinsurgency operations. The first airframe arrived at Will Rogers in June 2025, and test and instructor pilots have spent the past year preparing the “schoolhouse” to train special ops aviators.
According to flight tracking data, the OA-1K involved in the incident took off from Will Rogers in the mid-afternoon of Oct. 5 and flew patterns for several hours before coming in to land at Sundance Airport. About midway down the runway, the aircraft veered to its left and came to rest in the grass.
“The 492nd Special Operations Wing is tracking an incident involving one of its OA-1K Skyraider II aircraft at Sundance Airport, Oklahoma City,” the wing spokesperson said. “Both crew members are safe and the cause of the incident is under investigation. Further details will follow as the investigation develops.”
Citing the Oklahoma City Fire Department, local TV station News 9 reported that the aircraft “nose-dived” as it was landing and its propeller was damaged. Another TV station, KOCO News 5, released video of the aircraft after the incident, appearing to show its propeller blades bent and skid marks in the grass behind it.
The 492nd spokesperson said that, as of the morning of Oct. 6, the aircraft remains at Sundance Airport.
“Our team is currently working courses of action to remove the aircraft off the airfield. Safety-trained personnel are on scene documenting and collecting all evidence while developing a plan to remove the aircraft as soon as safety-investigative procedures allow,” the spokesperson said.
While the OA-1K formal training unit just started its first class of new pilots, this is the second safety incident involving the Skyraider II since it arrived in Oklahoma. In October 2025, an experienced special ops aviator making the transition to the OA-1K inadvertently shut off the plane’s fuel in the middle of a training sortie, leading to the aircraft flying extremely low over a local road before crashing in a field.

Air Force’s Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile Has First Flight Test
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
21:36:49 UTC
06:36:49 KST

The U.S. Air Force has conducted the first flight test release of its developing hypersonic cruise missile, with that test taking place in Australia.
An Air Force spokesperson confirmed to Air & Space Forces Magazine on Oct. 6 that the Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile flight test had occurred. The spokesperson did not specify a date.
The HACM flight test happened over a “designated Australian test range, gathering crucial data to advance the program’s objectives,” according to the spokesperson. The Woomera Test Range in the desert of southern Australia is commonly used to test missiles, aircraft, and projectiles.
The War Zone first reported on the test on Oct. 5.
“This effort is part of the Southern Cross Integrated Flight Research Experiment, a collaborative agreement built on more than 15 years of partnership between our two nations,” the spokesperson wrote in an email.
The spokesperson declined to provide further details regarding the method of test, platform used to conduct the test, flight times, durations, or speed.
RTX, the prime contractor on the missile, deferred any comments to the Air Force. Northrop Grumman, the missile’s engine-maker, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
HACM came out of a Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency program to develop a concept for a hypersonic air-breathing weapon and traces its origins to the Boeing X-51 Wave Rider project.
In April 2020, the Air Force issued an industry call for proposals on the potential weapon. It formally established the HACM program in 2022, picking RTX for the munition and Northrop for the scramjet engine.
HACM is one of two hypersonic weapons the Air Force is pursuing, along with the larger AGM-183 Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, or ARRW.
The munition uses a conventional rocket booster to reach high speeds, then ditches it and engages the scramjet engine to reach and maintain speeds above Mach 5, or 3,300 miles per hour, at high altitudes.
HACM recently saw a yearlong delay because of design problems, and the Air Force cut its flight count for rapid-prototyping tests from seven to five. A 2024 GAO report said the program had a “zero margin” in its development timeline at the time, and it has since been declared behind schedule and over its original budget.
USAF is seeking about $1.2 billion to mature and field the missile in its fiscal 2027 budget proposal. It has also asked for a dedicated production line for the missile and requested $404 million for the first operational lot.
The Air Force plans to begin fielding HACM in fiscal 2027 and expects to move it to full-rate production by fiscal 2029.

Between the Energy Crisis and New Trade Challenges,” organized by the Italian Embassy in Madrid at the Consulate General on the occasion of the international Fruit Attraction trade fair, held October 6–8 at the IFEMA complex in the Spanish capital.
                                    
The discussion brought together representatives from the leading organizations in the Italian agri-food sector to address business prospects, market access, and new challenges to competitiveness, including the energy crisis, innovation, and climate change.

    For D’Eramo, innovation and investment must enable businesses to cope with rising energy costs, conflicts, and the effects of climate change, thereby strengthening the sector’s competitiveness.

Meanwhile, 108 companies are part of the collective organized by ICE, the Agency for the Promotion Abroad and Internationalization of Italian Enterprises.
                                    
“This participation clearly demonstrates our sector’s international outlook and the willingness of companies to engage with markets, meet new partners, consolidate the potential of commercial relationships, and, above all, seize new growth opportunities in a region and market such as Spain,” emphasized Buccino Grimaldi. 
    The ambassador highlighted the strength of economic and trade relations between Italy and Spain. These are countries that “share certain priorities,” including the call on the EU for “a strong and adequately funded Common Agricultural Policy, an ever-greater focus on the competitiveness and profitability of agricultural businesses—in a geopolitical and climatic context that is not always favorable—and a simpler European framework capable of supporting investment and innovation.”

Zein Khalil and Mohammad Sio
07 October 2026•Update: 07 October 2026
 Israel’s Central Elections Committee has ordered Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for a second time, to pay legal costs and remove a video from his personal social media accounts after ruling that footage filmed at a military base amounted to “election propaganda.”
Israel’s Channel 7 reported Tuesday that committee chairman Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg ordered Netanyahu to delete a video filmed at Tel Nof Air Base from his personal accounts and pay 2,500 shekels (about $821) in costs.
Sohlberg found that publishing the video on Netanyahu’s personal accounts violated election law because it used public resources, including a military base and an Israeli Air Force aircraft, according to the broadcaster.
The ruling, however, allowed Netanyahu to keep the video on his official accounts.
Netanyahu posted the video from Tel Nof Air Base in central Israel on Sept. 29, with an Israeli Air Force aircraft visible in the background.
In the clip, he warned that Israel could face attacks ahead of the election, saying there were “indications that our enemies will try to attack us before the elections,” according to Israel’s Channel 15.
The decision came after Sohlberg on Sunday accepted five petitions against Netanyahu concerning the use of official speeches and the Israeli military for election propaganda on his personal social media accounts.
The petitions included a video showing Netanyahu during a visit to an Israeli military position in southern Lebanon.
Sohlberg ruled that the edited clip focused on the achievements of the government and prime minister, while parts relating to boosting soldiers’ morale and honoring them had been removed.
“This is, of course, election propaganda,” the committee chairman said.
He ordered Netanyahu to remove the posts and pay 29,000 shekels (about $9,000) in costs.
Israel is scheduled to hold a Knesset election on Oct. 27, with parties in Netanyahu’s governing coalition, led by his Likud party, competing against opposition parties.
Recent polls have not shown either bloc independently securing the 61 seats needed to form a government.
A poll by Israel’s public broadcaster KAN on Sunday gave opposition parties 52 seats compared with 51 for Netanyahu’s coalition.
Netanyahu has headed the current government since late December 2022 -- a government described as the most right-wing in Israel's history.
He is standing trial on corruption charges, which he denies, while the International Criminal Court has issued an arrest warrant for him over war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza.

Germany's former spy chief detained on suspicion of trading state secrets
Former German spy chief August Hanning was detained Tuesday on suspicion of treason and espionage after prosecutors accused him of paying for secret intelligence documents and using them to prepare an analysis for a foreign intelligence service, in a case that could strain Berlin’s ties with allied spy agencies.
To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
Former German spy chief August Hanning was detained on Tuesday on suspicion of attempted treason in a case that ranks among Germany's biggest intelligence scandals since the Cold War.
Prosecutors accused him of paying for secret documents and using them in an analysis for a foreign spy service. They did not identify the intelligence service and it was not immediately clear whether the analysis reached its intended recipient.
The arrest of a former head of Germany's foreign intelligence is unprecedented and could damage the country's intelligence relationships with allied nations, according to a senior security lawmaker.
"Hanning is strongly suspected of treasonous espionage, obtaining state secrets, attempted treason and espionage," the prosecutor's office said in a statement.
The Spiegel news magazine reported late on Tuesday that investigators were pursuing a possible connection to Azerbaijan. It reported Hanning had been in contact with an agent from the country.

One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
The federal prosecutor's office declined to comment on the report.
Hanning did not respond to a request for comment. The chancellery declined to comment.
Five years after his seven-year tenure as head of the BND foreign intelligence service ended in 2005, Hanning agreed with a former BND office manager to receive confidential intelligence information in exchange for payment, according to prosecutors.
The office manager, identified as Manfred D. in line with privacy rules, was also arrested on Tuesday, and both were due to appear before a judge at the Federal Court of Justice.
Manfred D. served as office manager to successive BND presidents until March 2026, potentially giving him access to some of Germany's most current intelligence at the time that prosecutors say documents were being siphoned from the service.
Read more‘Russian sleeper cell’: Can Germany’s far-right AfD be barred from sensitive intel?
'No compromises'
Prosecutors said D. is suspected of having supplied around 2,000 documents over the years, including classified material intended solely for internal use within the BND and senior-level intelligence briefings at the chancellery.
Those included documents relating to the Iranian nuclear programme and the Russian military, as well as highly sensitive material classified as secret by allied intelligence agencies in other countries, Sueddeutsche Zeitung (SZ) newspaper reported.
Prosecutors said Hanning had used classified information supplied by D. to prepare an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service and for years shared political information with a representative of the spy agency.
The case does not involve Russia, according to information obtained by Sueddeutsche Zeitung.
Conservative security expert Roderich Kiesewetter told the Handelsblatt newspaper on Tuesday that the case could strain relations with Germany's intelligence allies, saying espionage cases of this kind were "particularly burdensome for trust and particularly damaging for Germany".
BND President Martin Jaeger said the agency had launched extensive internal investigations as soon as suspicions emerged, adding, "There can be no compromises on internal security."
Read moreGermany arrests Ukrainian national accused of spying on defence firm
Past spy scandals
Hanning's arrest is the latest in a series of notorious espionage scandals in Germany.
West German Chancellor Willy Brandt was forced to resign in 1974 after it was revealed that an East German spy had worked as his close aide for nearly two years. In 1990, senior West German counter-intelligence official Klaus Kuron was exposed as a Stasi spy and later convicted of treason.
More recently, former domestic intelligence chief Hans-Georg Maassen said in 2024 he was being monitored by the security agency he once ran over alleged right-wing political extremism, which he denied.

CNN, CBS News now under one roof as Paramount-Warner Bros merger closes
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
21:33:59 UTC
06:33:59 KST

CNN, CBS News now under one roof as Paramount-Warner Bros merger closes
The newly combined company is called Skydance and began trading on Wall Street on Tuesday
Paramount Skydance has completed its $110bn merger with Warner Bros Discovery to form Skydance.
The deal, which closed on Tuesday, brings together two entertainment giants that own movie studios and theme parks, but also brings two of the United States’ most influential news brands under one roof — CNN and CBS News.
Skydance CEO David Ellison, son of tech tycoon Larry Ellison, who is also a close ally of US President Donald Trump, has appointed Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO. Kreiz previously led Mattel.
The road to the merger has included lawsuits from unions and 12 different state attorneys general. But the deal was ultimately settled after the company agreed to appoint an independent editorial board to oversee both news networks amid concerns that the merger would lead to skewed coverage at the two networks.
On Monday, the company announced that Mark Thompson will stay on as CNN’s editor-in-chief, while Bari Weiss, editor-in-chief at CBS News, who was appointed to the role a year ago on Monday, will stay in her position.
Thompson’s continuation brought “a sigh of relief” among journalists at CNN, its media industry newsletter, Reliable Sources, reported.
Ever since the merger had been announced, there had been a wave of concerns at the network that major changes would be made to CNN if the Ellisons took over.
A looming future
There are still a lot of unknowns about what news will look like under Skydance. In a memo to staffers on Monday, Thompson said that “the specifics of how CNN will plug into and operate in the new company have yet to be finalized.”
That means looming fears of layoffs and consolidation still weigh on both news divisions as the combined company will carry $80bn in debt, while the entertainment giants look to cut costs, grow their streaming footprint and have pledged to produce 30 movies per year.
Thompson’s stay may be temporary, as The New York Times reported that his contract is up in the spring.
It is also not yet clear whether the networks will stay separate or combine in the long term, amid concerns that CBS News’ Weiss could be handed additional charge of CNN. In the past, the network’s top talent, including journalist Anderson Cooper, has threatened to leave if she came on board.
Weiss took over the network one year ago, and viewership has slumped across the board. Most recently, the news magazine programme 60 Minutes saw viewership slump during its season premiere last month, dropping 21 percent from the prior year and marking its worst viewership for a season premiere in 25 years, according to Nielsen ratings.
Editorial questions
The terms of the attorneys general’s lawsuit settlement require an independent editorial oversight board for both the networks. Skydance has 180 days to put it together. Press freedom experts do not believe that will help maintain editorial independence.
“It doesn’t take effect for 180 days. The newsroom can be totally overhauled in 180 days,” Seth Stern, director of advocacy for the Freedom of the Press Foundation, told Al Jazeera.
It is not the first time a publication has appointed an editorial board to weigh in on concerns about editorial influence. In 2007, when News Corp acquired Dow Jones, the parent company of the Wall Street Journal, the Bancroft family, which owned the publisher at the time, was concerned that new owner and media mogul Rupert Murdoch would impact the paper’s editorial independence with his conservative tilt.
The paper appointed a five-person independent committee to preserve editorial integrity. But it was later revealed, including by former members of the board during a roundtable discussion hosted by the Freedom of the Press Foundation, that it did not deliver the oversight that it was originally intended to provide.
In Skydance’s case, the board is to be made up of five journalists appointed by Ellison, and there is no requirement for the company to disclose its findings to the public. The terms say that no more than two people on the board can be affiliated with the same political party.
“The truth isn’t dictated by the fifty-yard line between political parties. Sometimes neither political party is even close to the truth. So having a commitment to bipartisan representation, as opposed to a commitment to truth-telling, totally misunderstands what news is,” Stern said.
On Wall Street, the new company began trading under the ticker symbol SKYD. Since opening on Tuesday, the stock has dropped 2.5 percent.

Indonesia Tightens Health Checks After Suspected Plague-Linked Death in Russia

Indonesia Tightens Health Checks After Suspected Plague-Linked Death in Russia
Indonesia has tightened health surveillance at international airports and seaports after reports that a laboratory worker in Russia died from pneumonia suspected of being linked to plague, Antara reported on October 6.
Aji Muhawarman, head of Indonesia’s Health Ministry Bureau of Communication and Public Information, stated that authorities were closely monitoring developments and strengthening preparedness at entry points.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The measures followed the death of a 28-year-old employee of Russia’s Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia. Russian authorities described the cause as “pneumonia of unknown etiology” and said testing found no microorganisms linked to her work.
Antara noted that Indonesia had received no notification through the International Health Regulations National Focal Point or the World Health Organization’s Event Information Site requiring special vigilance.
Despite the absence of an international alert, authorities increased checks at airports and seaports, including in Bali. Measures include health declarations through the SATUSEHAT Health Pass system, symptom monitoring, risk-based assessments of arriving vessels, and surveillance of rodents and fleas.
Travelers showing symptoms including fever, coughing, or shortness of breath may be referred to designated infectious disease hospitals for isolation and treatment, the report added.
Nearly 200 people who had been in contact with the employee were reportedly placed under medical observation while the investigation continued.
The increased screening is particularly relevant for Indonesia because of the volume of Russian tourism. The Moscow Times reported, citing the Association of Russian Tour Operators, that Indonesia remains one of the main Asian destinations for Russian travelers, with 129,672 Russian tourists visiting Bali in the first half of 2026, just 2% below the record set during the same period in 2025.
Days earlier, reports from Russia indicated that the employee may have been exposed on September 25 after breaking a test tube containing the pneumonic plague pathogen, though this was never officially confirmed.
Authorities subsequently quarantined a hospital in Shelekhov, while public warnings mentioning plague were later removed from some Russian outlets and local channels.
Russian media reported a second death on October 6 amid the suspected plague outbreak in the Irkutsk region, although the claim has not been independently confirmed. Russian health authorities continue to deny that an outbreak is occurring, while several reports mentioning plague have reportedly been removed from Russian media.

The Ministry of Internal Affairs explained what to do during an attack on the road and where to take shelter
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-07
00:30:45 EEST
06:30:45 KST

The Ministry of Internal Affairs explained what to do during an attack on the road and where to take shelter
Kyiv • UNN
The Ministry of Internal Affairs advises leaving your vehicle during shelling and seeking a depression in the ground. It is dangerous to hide under bridges, in cars, or on the roadside.
The Ministry of Internal Affairs (MIA) has provided advice on what to do if an attack catches a person on the road. This was reported by UNN.
Details
It is noted that if shelling begins while traveling on public transport, one should ask the driver to stop, exit the vehicle, and move as far away as possible from the road and structures that could collapse. One should not remain inside the vehicle during shelling, as public transport does not provide adequate protection.
If an attack catches you while driving
Drivers are advised to stop the car and leave it. Attempting to drive out of the shelling zone at high speed is not recommended.
After leaving the car, one should move away from it and find the nearest safe depression. A car does not protect a person from shrapnel and may catch fire.
Why you should not hide under a bridge
The MIA warns against attempting to wait out shelling under bridges and overpasses. Such structures are not safe shelters, as they may be damaged or collapse as a result of a strike.
If a person is in an area where active hostilities previously took place, they must not stop on the roadside. Explosive objects may remain there, so it is necessary to pay attention to warning signs.
What to do if there is no shelter nearby
If it is impossible to reach a shelter quickly, one should find the nearest depression and lie in it face down.
You should:
-  cross your legs; 
-  cover your head with your hands; 
-  close your eyes; 
-  open your mouth. 
If a child is nearby, adults are advised to cover the child with their bodies. One should not raise their head unless absolutely necessary. As soon as the opportunity arises, one should move to the nearest shelter.
We remind you
The Ministry of Education and Science has prepared recommendations for educational institutions of various levels in case of power outages and other crisis situations.

Best Prime Day Digital Wall Calendar Deals: Skylight, Everblog, Apolosign (2026)
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
21:30:41 UTC
06:30:41 KST

I test a slew of devices every year, but it’s rare that a category truly surprises me. I entered the world of digital wall calendars expecting to hate them, and I walked away their biggest fan. If you’ve been curious about getting one for yourself, now is the perfect time: Just about all of my picks are on sale.
If you’re unfamiliar, a digital wall calendar is a physical device that syncs all of your digital calendars onto its screen. No more grabbing your phone to check when the next appointment is or scribbling out plans that fell through. It’s great for couples and families who juggle multiple schedules and want to see them all in one place, on a screen the entire family can access.
But these devices don’t stop there. All my picks also act as an overall family hub, managing chores, meal plans, and more to make life a little easier. It’s the smartest device in my kitchen, though it isn’t a true smart-home device.
Here’s a collection of the best digital wall calendars I’ve tried and their sale prices for Amazon Prime Big Deal Days 2026. You can also check out my guide for more details, and don’t miss all our deal roundups this season.
The Best On-Sale Digital Calendars
The best deal is on Everblog’s HomeCal, which feels surprisingly similar to the popular Skylight Calendar without requiring a subscription to access every feature. The 21.5-inch device is often discounted from its $400 price tag to around $320, but you can get it for $280 at the time of writing.
I really like that this calendar has all the features I could want without any paywalls. You’ll get meal planning, chores, and to-dos on top of calendars, and you can also have it double as a digital photo frame for free. You can only upload one photo at a time, but a slower experience is well worth not paying a subscription fee.
If you’re looking to spend even less and still avoid a subscription fee, the Apolosign Digital Calendar is a great choice that’s also on sale for Prime Day. It’s available for the cheapest price out of my picks—just $249—with a 15.6-inch screen and options for either Apolosign’s Calendar Mode or Android Mode, which gives you more customization tools.
The Android Mode will allow you to add a photo screensaver so it can also function as a digital photo frame. This view makes it less calendar-focused, however; it feels more like an Android tablet. You’ll get to customize widgets, but it doesn’t sync as smoothly on this mode.
My all-around favorite digital wall calendar comes from Skylight, but my preferred option—the Skylight Calendar 2 with a 15.6-inch screen—has only certain colors on sale. It’s usually available on Skylight’s website for $300, though, so this discount isn’t outrageous. The Skylight Calendar Max, with its massive 27-inch screen, is on sale for a nice discount, but even this price is more than twice Apolosign’s, and some features are paywalled.
Still, it’s a great device, and Skylight’s original product is digital photo frames, so it’s no surprise that the photo feature works best on this one compared to other frames. The interface feels clean on both the device and companion app, syncs fairly seamlessly with my variety of calendars, and updates on its own with new features (and will give me a fun pop-up the next morning telling me what's new). I just wish it didn’t have a paywall and that the smaller, better-priced Calendar 2 had a bigger sale.

Tennessee execution survivor Christa Pike is conscious and speaking, lawyers say
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
21:29:03 UTC
06:29:03 KST

US execution survivor Christa Pike is conscious and speaking, lawyers say
- - Christa Pike, 50, has regained consciousness and is speaking after Tennessee’s failed lethal injection attempt, her lawyers said on 6 October.
- - Pike suffered severe arm injuries and remains handcuffed and shackled in hospital while receiving critical medical care.
- - The case follows the 1990 murder of Colleen Slemmer and makes Pike the first known person in the US to survive execution drugs.
AI generated
WASHINGTON - Convicted killer Christa Pike, who survived Tennessee’s effort to execute her by lethal injection last week, foiling the state’s first attempt to put a woman to death in two centuries, has regained consciousness and is speaking, her lawyers said in a statement on Oct 6.
Despite severe injuries to her arms from the insertion of intravenous lines during the aborted execution on Sept 30, Pike, 50, is “still handcuffed and shackled” to her hospital bed while she remains under medical care, her team of public defence attorneys wrote.
“Her prognosis remains unclear, but at a minimum we expect a long recovery,” the lawyers’ statement said, adding that a court hearing on Pike’s case was scheduled for Oct 7 in Davidson County Chancery Court.
The hearing pertains to her lawyers’ request for a court order to preserve evidence from the failed execution they said would show the Tennessee Department of Correction violated Pike’s constitutional rights by subjecting her to cruel and unusual punishment, a spokesperson said.
She was not expected to appear for the proceeding.
Pike, sentenced to death for her role in the torture-murder of 19-year-old schoolmate Colleen Slemmer three decades ago, survived the execution attempt on the night of Sept 30 at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital. She has been hospitalised since then.
Her lawyers said on Oct 2 that their client remained unconscious, critically ill and hooked to a ventilator to breathe, as doctors laboured to clear the drug pentobarbital from her system.
“Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking and continues to receive critical medical care,” they wrote on Oct 6.
Pike’s petition for clemency, denied last week by Republican Governor Bill Lee, argued her death sentence had failed to properly account for Pike’s own childhood trauma as the victim of sexual abuse, neglect and untreated mental illness.
Long the only woman on death row in the state, Pike also has endured nearly 30 years of solitary confinement, her lawyers say.
Pike went from being the first woman Tennessee had tried to put to death since the early 19th century to becoming the first person in the United States known to have survived after execution drugs were administered.
Death penalty opponents said the incident exposed the inherent barbarity of executions. It also highlighted the difficulties of carrying out lethal injections while respecting constitutional prohibitions on cruel and unusual punishment.
Lethal injection gone awry
Pike’s attorneys and journalists who witnessed the execution attempt described it as roughly 2½ hours of disarray and prolonged distress for her as Correction Department personnel struggled to administer two doses of pentobarbital intravenously.
Pike was heard gasping, crying, whimpering and breathing loudly through much of the procedure, at one point saying, “My arm feels like it’s about to burst open.”
The bungled attempt to establish intravenous lines left both of Pike’s arms “swollen, burned and blistered”, the apparent result of the pentobarbital, a highly alkaline and caustic substance, seeping into the tissues under her skin, her lawyers said in court filings.
The lawyers accused state officials of having shrugged off prior warnings from Pike’s doctors that her small veins and a blood disorder would make placing IV lines especially difficult.
In the midst of the procedure, Pike’s lawyers filed an emergency court motion to halt it. By then, prison officials had ceased their execution efforts and called an ambulance, according to court records.
The night of the execution attempt, the Correction Department defended its handling of the situation, saying it had “followed every step of the state’s lawful, established execution protocol”.
But agency commissioner Frank Strada has resigned and will leave his post in October, the governor announced on Oct 3.
Lee had previously ordered a suspension of any scheduled executions for the rest of 2026 and a third-party review of what happened in Pike’s case.
30-year saga
Two days before Pike was due to meet her fate, Lee rejected a petition seeking to commute her death penalty to a life prison term without the possibility of parole.
Pike was 18 in January 1995 when she, her 17-year-old boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, and a third companion lured Slemmer into a wooded area on the University of Tennessee campus in Knoxville and killed her.
The gruesome nature of the slaying, which involved Shipp carving the shape of a pentagram in the victim’s chest and Pike bashing Slemmer in the head with a chunk of asphalt, then taking a piece of her skull as a souvenir, drew intense media coverage at the time. Trial testimony indicated Pike viewed Slemmer as a rival for her boyfriend’s affections.
Pike and Shipp confessed to the killing, and both were convicted of first-degree murder. Pike was sentenced to death, while Shipp received a life sentence with the possibility of parole.
Their co-defendant, Shadolla Peterson, who was 18 at the time of the murder and had acted as a lookout for the other two, testified for the prosecution and received probation. REUTERS

US arrests suspect in connection with Tumbler Ridge school shooting
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
21:28:35 UTC
06:28:35 KST

US arrests suspect in connection with Tumbler Ridge school shooting
The suspect, from the western state of Washington, allegedly gave money and advice to the attacker over the internet.
Law enforcement in the northwestern United States have charged a suspect in connection with a deadly shooting at a Canadian school in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia.
On Tuesday, prosecutors charged 30-year-old James Cody Bryant, a resident of Washington state, with conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country.
Bryant allegedly provided money and technical advice to the attacker in conversations over the internet, starting six months before the February 10 attack.
The shooting was “a horrific tragedy for that small community and for all of Canada”, acting US Attorney Neil Floyd said at a news conference in Seattle. “Indeed, here in the Pacific Northwest, we felt the pain of those families devastated by this violence.”
Canadian officials have described the attack as one of the country’s worst mass shootings.
The suspect, 18-year-old transgender woman Jesse Van Rootselaar, shot and killed her mother and half-brother at their home before travelling to the Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and opening fire.
Six people were killed, including five students, and 27 other victims were injured. Van Rootselaar, a former student at the school, died by suicide at the end of the attack.
Police in Canada said at the time that Van Rootselaar had a history of mental health issues.
Alleged online advice and financial support
US prosecutors allege Bryant and Van Rootselaar had been in touch through the social media service Discord and had discussed how to carry out the mass shooting.
The pair discussed how to maximise notoriety after the attack, with Bryant allegedly agreeing to livestream it through Twitch, Floyd said on Tuesday.
Bryant also allegedly provided money for items like a pair of shoes for the attack and instructed Van Rootselaar on how to start and then drive a car to reach the school.
Prosecutors alleged Bryant, whom officials cited by The Associated Press and Reuters say identifies as female, had admitted to investigators that she was “maybe the only one who could have stopped the shooter”.
Warning signs ignored
In September, the British Columbia government sued the technology company OpenAI in a California court, saying its ChatGPT platform played a role in the shooting.
Van Rootselaar, the Canadian officials alleged, had been flagged by OpenAI’s safety team for her statements about gun violence, and her account had been suspended. But law enforcement authorities were not alerted to the problem.
In its lawsuit, British Columbia sought financial compensation from the company to cover its emergency response to the shooting and community recovery efforts.
It also asked the court to force OpenAI to reform how it identifies and handles users who threaten violence.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he was “deeply sorry” his company had not contacted law enforcement in a public letter two months after the shooting.
“While I know words can never be enough, I believe an apology is necessary to recognize the harm and irreversible loss your community has suffered,” he wrote, adding that OpenAI would take steps to prevent such “tragedies” in the future.
The lawsuit filed in California alleges Altman’s company never undertook the promised policy changes.
By the time of the filing, OpenAI was facing more than 30 other lawsuits in California, where it is based, from victims’ families, survivors and others affected by the Tumbler Ridge attack over alleged negligence.

NAIROBI, Oct. 6 (Xinhua) -- Kenya on Tuesday confirmed its first case of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, in a patient who has since died, prompting the government to heighten vigilance amid an ongoing outbreak in the northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).
Cabinet Secretary for Health Aden Duale confirmed that the case involved a Kenyan national who had been residing in the DRC for the past seven years.
"The patient fell ill about a month ago and received treatment at several hospitals in the DRC. He travelled by road to Kampala (Uganda) before boarding a flight to Nairobi, arriving Oct. 3," Duale said at a press conference in Nairobi, the Kenyan capital.
He said that the patient presented with symptoms including fever, chills, fatigue, muscle pain, painful swallowing, a sore throat, and subcutaneous bleeding before being admitted, isolated, and evaluated at a hospital in Nairobi.
Laboratory analysis conducted by Kenya's National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI) confirmed the presence of Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the patient died on Monday night and was buried on Tuesday in line with the country's Ebola safe and dignified burial protocol.
The Ministry of Health has identified 28 contact persons, comprising family members and healthcare workers who attended to the patient, and is currently tracing 23 passengers and four crew members who traveled on the same flight.
Duale assured the public that Kenya has strong systems to contain the virus.
He urged citizens to remain calm, rely on official Ministry of Health updates, and seek immediate medical attention if they experience any symptoms.
The official said Kenya has maintained heightened Ebola surveillance since the outbreak began in the DRC in May.
As of Oct. 6, health authorities have screened 652,584 incoming travelers and processed 267 samples across five reference laboratories, with only the single confirmed positive case to date.
In addition, he highlighted that 4,971 healthcare workers across national and county levels have undergone specialized training in Ebola prevention, infection control, and case management.
Patrick Amoth, Director-General for Health in Kenya's Ministry of Health, explained that the incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days.
Consequently, individuals undergoing quarantine or contact monitoring are isolated for up to 21 days to prevent potential transmission.
"If anyone develops symptoms within this period, the person will be transported from the incubation site to an Ebola treatment unit for care," he said as he elaborated Kenya's preparedness.
Ahmed Idris, Secretary General of the Kenya Red Cross Society, confirmed that the charity has activated its specialized Safe and Dignified Burial (SDB) teams, community engagement units, and community-based surveillance volunteers to support the national emergency response.
Regional airline Jambojet, which operated the flight that carried the patient from Entebbe, the airport serving the Ugandan capital Kampala, to Nairobi, said it is working closely with the Ministry of Health, port health services and aviation authorities to assist with contact tracing and response measures.
Korir Sing'Oei, Kenya's principal secretary in the Ministry of Foreign and Diaspora Affairs, described the confirmed Ebola case as regrettable, noting that it underscores the strength and necessity of the containment capabilities established by the government to handle public health emergencies.
Kenya's Ministry of Health confirmed it has formally notified WHO of the case in compliance with International Health Regulations (IHR).
WHO declared the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the DRC and in Uganda a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) in May, calling for international coordination and resource mobilization.
According to the health agency, the outbreak continues to unfold against a complex epidemiological and security backdrop marked by population mobility, cross-border trade, and large displaced communities.
As of Oct. 2, the DRC's Ministry of Health reported more than 8,000 confirmed cases and at least 4,000 fatalities linked to the Bundibugyo strain, with transmission primarily concentrated across the DRC and neighboring regional trade corridors. ■

====================================================================================================

Explainer: Why neutrinos matter as Francis Halzen wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics?
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-07
05:24:52 CST
06:24:52 KST

STOCKHOLM, Oct. 6 (Xinhua) -- Buried deep beneath the Antarctic ice, thousands of light sensors wait for flashes left by neutrinos, elusive particles that can travel across the universe almost undisturbed.
By turning a cubic kilometre of South Pole ice into a giant detector, physicist Francis Halzen helped open a new window on the cosmos.
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded Halzen the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics on Tuesday "for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin."
WHAT ARE NEUTRINOS, AND WHY DO THEY MATTER?
Neutrinos are among the smallest known particles. They carry no electric charge, have extremely little mass, and interact so weakly with matter that most pass straight through the Earth without leaving a trace.
Olle Eriksson, a member of the Nobel Committee for Physics and professor at Uppsala University, told Xinhua that detecting neutrinos is extremely challenging: "Through my thumbnail, there are 65 billion neutrinos that go through every second, and I don't feel it." But once detected, they can reveal information about events occurring far out in the universe.
Scientists have long known that the cosmos contains natural particle accelerators capable of producing particles with energies far beyond those achievable in laboratories on Earth. The origins of the highest-energy cosmic particles, however, have remained difficult to trace.
Cosmic rays carry electric charge and are deflected by magnetic fields as they travel through space. Neutrinos, unlike other particles, are electrically neutral and travel essentially in a straight line, allowing scientists to trace their direction back toward the violent environments where they were produced.
HOW DID HALZEN TURN SOUTH POLE ICE INTO A TELESCOPE?
In 1988, Halzen, the Belgian-born scientist, presented the idea of installing light sensors deep in Antarctic ice. When one of the rare neutrinos collides with an atomic nucleus, it can produce a charged particle that generates a faint flash of blue light as it moves through the transparent ice. Sensors can capture that light and help scientists reconstruct where the neutrino came from.
The idea eventually became IceCube, a detector using an entire cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice. Completed in 2011, it contains 5,160 light sensors, mostly between about 1,450 and 2,450 metres below the surface.
The depth matters. "There, the ice is very clear, no air bubbles, no dirt, no dust," said Eriksson, adding that this condition allows faint flashes to travel hundreds of metres before being absorbed.
The effort paid off. In 2013, IceCube researchers reported the first strong evidence for high-energy neutrinos arriving from distant space. With more data, they were able to establish that some of the particles originated far outside the solar system.
Eriksson said the achievement helps humanity better understand its surroundings and its place in the universe by providing information about extreme cosmic events that cannot easily be obtained in other ways.
The immediate significance lies mainly in expanding fundamental knowledge, he said, adding that major scientific discoveries can also lead to practical applications that were impossible to foresee when the research began.
WHY HALZEN, AND WHAT COMES NEXT?
IceCube is the work of a large international collaboration involving hundreds of scientists and engineers. "Even though it is a large collaboration, we could still identify one person who was the pivotal, most important contributor to that experimental buildup and the experimental discovery," said Eriksson.
"It was a long journey, but ... it finally worked," Halzen recalled the early phases at Tuesday's Nobel press conference, describing how the success was not guaranteed nearly 40 years ago but made possible by critical contributions from many people.
The journey is continuing. Scientists are planning IceCube-Gen2, which is expected to expand the instrumented volume at the South Pole to about eight cubic kilometres, while other neutrino observatories are being developed around the world.
Halzen said opening a new window on the universe often leads to unexpected discoveries. For neutrino astronomy, that window may only have begun to open. ■

Scientists develop method to generate green hydrogen while producing valuable chemicals
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-07
05:24:21 CST
06:24:21 KST

JERUSALEM, Oct. 6 (Xinhua) -- Israeli and Chinese scientists have developed a method to generate green hydrogen while simultaneously producing valuable chemicals for industry, the Israel Institute of Technology said in a statement Tuesday.
In their study, published in Nature Communications, the researchers described a new approach that could help make green hydrogen production more affordable.
Green hydrogen is made by using electricity, ideally from renewable sources such as solar and wind, to split water into hydrogen and oxygen.
The researchers developed a process that replaces the oxygen normally produced alongside hydrogen with an epoxide, a chemical compound used to make plastics, coatings, adhesives, medicines, and other industrial products.
According to the team, the new process achieved 98 percent efficiency in both hydrogen production and the parallel chemical reaction, and the system reached a current density suitable for large-scale industrial electrolysis. ■

Armed individuals from Belarus threaten Latvian soldiers at border, followed by another breach

NEW DELHI: Captain Smit Machchhar's heroic act of saving flydubai FZ1073 has acquired another dimension with the extent of the injuries he was fighting to save the plane from its suicidal Omani co-pilot now coming out.Sources say co-pilot Hammam al-Hammami hitting him with the axe kept in the cockpit had led to a "depressed fracture fragment of skull". An emergency surgery is learnt to have been performed in Saudi Arabia before Captain Machchhar could be flown back to the UAE for further treatment.
Dr (Air Cmde) Krishan Kumar Yadav, senior clinical director and professor of neurosurgery and neuro-spine surgery at Marengo Asia Hospitals, told TOI: "A depressed skull fracture is serious. Put simply, a piece of the skull has been pressed inward toward the brain. During surgery, doctors make a careful incision, lift or remove the pressed-in fragment, and check the protective membrane around the brain for tears. They clean the area, repair any damage, and then either replace the bone or reconstruct it. It is delicate work, but it is work we are trained for, and many patients do very well afterwards."The Indian embassy in the UAE said on X Tuesday: "Capt Smit continues to make steady progress and is regaining his health.
The embassy remains in close touch with his family, doctors and local authorities, extending all possible assistance. We thank everyone for their prayers & wish him a speedy recovery.""Recovery is not a straight line. The first days are quiet ones: rest, careful monitoring, and keeping him comfortable. Then, bit by bit, strength returns. There will be good days and slower ones. Headaches, tiredness, or trouble concentrating are common while the body heals, and they don't mean something is wrong," Dr Yadav said.Captain Machchhar had told Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu: "It was a normal flight, and the co-pilot wanted to pray, which a lot of locals do. While he was praying, out of respect, I just looked at the front and not at the back." He said that about four or five minutes later, he suddenly felt a heavy blow to the back of his head, which he initially thought was an impact involving the aircraft.
"After about four or five minutes, my first thought was damage to the aircraft and something is not right. But then the blow kept coming, one after the other. And that's when I realised that it's not the aircraft, it's the other guy who was in the cockpit with me."He tried to stop the co-pilot but was badly affected by the initial blows. "I did try to stop him, but because of his initial blows, my vision was almost like nothing. And I was completely blurred out," the captain said. He then realised the aircraft was descending sharply.

Essendon acquired Jack Bowes, who had requested a move to the club, a 2027 first-round selection and a 2028 second-round selection in exchange for Ridley, a fourth-round selection in this year's draft (currently No.60) and 2028 fourth-round pick.

Best Prime Day Laptop Deals: Save Up to $500 (2026)
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
21:15:00 UTC
06:15:00 KST

Laptop prices have risen significantly over the past six months. The memory shortage wreaked havoc on prices, even causing Apple to hike them up in June. That makes deals on big shopping events like Amazon Prime Day even more important. For the retailer's Prime Big Deal Days fall sale, I've spotted a number of my favorite laptops among the dozens I've already tested this year.
So, whether you're looking for a new MacBook or a budget Windows device, you'll find some excellent picks below. In addition, check out more deals in our roundup of the Absolute Prime Day Deals and Best Apple Prime Day Deals.
Updated 5:21 am ET October 7: We've added some deals on useful accessories and checked through all the laptop deals.
MacBook Air (M5)
The MacBook Air is $200 off for Prime Day, bringing it to $1,099. That's the cheapest it's been since June. It's a remarkable deal compared to the competition, especially given the 512 GB of storage and 16 GB of RAM it comes with. Apple raised prices across the board on Macs this past June, but this discount reverses that issue entirely. This sale is on the latest M5 model, which came out this past spring and performed really well in all my testing. It's currently at the top of my recommendations not only as the best MacBook but also as the best overall laptop of any kind. That $200 discount applies to every configuration of the MacBook Air available on Amazon, including the larger 15-inch model.
Not only is this the MacBook I recommend to buy for most people, it's also the best laptop deal this week. Neither the MacBook Neo nor the MacBook Pro are being discounted by anything out of the ordinary.
Microsoft Surface Laptop 13.8
This is the best price on the latest version of the Surface Laptop since it launched. I've been tracking it closely, primarily because of how expensive it has been in comparison to the older model from 2024. The price difference always made me recommend the 2024 version, even though it had a slower Snapdragon chip inside. This discount, which is $500 off the retail price and $70 cheaper than it's ever been, brings it close enough to the price of the 2024 model to justify itself. The Snapdragon X2 Elite's GPU performance compared to the X1 model is significant enough to justify the extra money.
For what it's worth, though, the 2024 Surface Laptop 13.8-inch model is currently selling for $1,096, which is also a great deal. If you're trying to get your purchase closer to $1,000, I still think that model is one of the best Windows laptops you can buy.
HP OmniBook 5
The HP OmniBook 5 has been my favorite budget laptop for a while now. It avoids so many of the pitfalls of cheap Windows devices, including typical low-end screens, thick chassis, and poor battery life. This one has a beautiful OLED screen, is as thin as a MacBook Neo, and gets fantastic battery life, thanks to the Snapdragon X chip inside. The one compromise is the touchpad, which still isn't very good.
HP.com typically has the lowest price, which is $780 right now. But Amazon has that beat during Prime Day, at only $750 for the 16-inch model. Not only is it cheaper, but it also comes with 512 GB of storage, twice the amount as the discounted HP.com model. I should say that I prefer the 14-inch model, just because the 1920 x 1200 resolution looks a bit sharper on it.
Lenovo LOQ 15
This has long since been one of my go-to affordable gaming laptops to recommend for two very important reasons. First off, most budget gaming laptops have terrible screens. That's true of the Alienware 15, the MSI Cyborg A16, and even the Lenovo LOQ 15 Essential Edition—all gaming laptops in the same price range as the Lenovo LOQ 15. But the LOQ 15 display has good color coverage, so greens and reds don't look oversaturated. With that benefit, the LOQ 15 still tends to cost less than its alternatives, and for Prime Day, the RTX 5050 configuration is as cheap as I've seen it in many, many months. If you can increase your budget, the $1,499 RTX 5060 model at Walmart will deliver much better gaming performance, and I'd recommend it too.
Asus ZenBook A14
The Asus Zenbook A14 is known for being super light. It weighs only 2.16 pounds, about half a pound lighter than the MacBook Air. The difference is really noticeable, both in the hand and when toting it around in a bag. It also comes with an OLED display, a great touchpad, and a decent assortment of ports.
But like the Surface Laptop, the 2026 Zenbook A14 is too expensive. Unlike the Surface Laptop, it's not on sale for Prime Day. That's why I'd recommend picking up the previous model, which comes with a Snapdragon X Plus, 16 GB of RAM, and 512 GB of storage. The 2026 model offers more storage options, but it also has a much higher starting price. A slightly cheaper model is also available with the Snapdragon X, but the Snapdragon X Plus offers better multicore CPU and GPU performance.

Lopez: 'Take out' L.A. or San Diego? This buffoon thinks Trump was way out of line
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

‘Take out’ L.A. or San Diego? This buffoon thinks Trump was way out of line
- Click here to listen to this article
-   Share via
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
- Maybe a gratuitous and unfunny line about anyone taking out American cities is better left unsaid.
- White House Communications Director Steven Cheung claimed Trump was misrepresented.
I went to bed at a decent hour Monday night and got a pretty good sleep.
I woke up refreshed Tuesday morning, only to see the news that President Trump seemed to have told a crowd in Nebraska that it wouldn’t be such a bad thing if Iran attacked Southern California.
“Let ’em take out Los Angeles. Let ’em take out San Diego,” he said in a typically meandering speech, perhaps trying to justify a war he has repeatedly claimed is keeping the U.S. safe, even as gas prices have spiked. “This is a very small price to pay.”
The Nebraska crowd cheered.
“San Diego is not collateral damage,” said San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria.
Such “dangerous” remarks could “potentially compromise our safety,” said L.A. Mayor Karen Bass.
“He is deranged and dangerous,” said Gov. Gavin Newsom.
About 8 a.m., I took my dog Philly out for our morning walk. This is usually a lovely time for us. I clear my head. For Philly, a 3-year-old beagle, these are essentially business trips.
I got to thinking about the similarities in the daily routines of Philly and the president of the United States.
The thing is, I carry bags with me and clean up after Philly. The president to my knowledge has nobody on his staff doing this. We are at a point in American politics at which we must consider posting signs, everywhere Trump travels, that say, “Please Curb Your President.”
Not that it would be easy to clean Trump’s daily messes. You’d need the equivalent of those parade attendants in overalls who run along behind the horses with shovels.
The White House does not use poop bags. Instead, it uses denial and spin.
Trump made the remarks during a rambling speech in which he said gas prices would be lower soon, touted his ouster of Venezuela’s dictator, and made attacks on news outlets.
Critical reactions to Trump’s Nebraska comments were “not rooted in reality,” said White House Director of Communications Steven Cheung, who claimed Trump was misrepresented.
We’ve got to respect Cheung’s opinion. Does anyone in the world have more experience when it comes to analyzing comments not rooted in reality?
Some of you may know there are two topics I often revisit in my column. One is the effects, good and bad, of aging. The other is failure of leadership.
So I feel eminently qualified to psychoanalyze the president.
I don’t mean to generalize, but as people age, it’s not unusual for them to undergo behavioral changes. Some folks mellow, they abide, they lean into the ride. Others can become churlish, combative or grouchy.
Not only is Trump the poster boy for the latter group, but as things go wrong, he becomes more obstinate.
And things have definitely gone wrong.
The war in Iran is a disaster. The president is personally responsible for rising gas prices. He’s ruined the economy with his tariffs. He’s picked a fight with Canada. He may cost his party the House and the Senate because his almost daily outrages have pumped oxygen back into the blood of long-slumping Democrats.
A normal person would have the good sense to scale back or shrink away.
Trump keeps doubling down, wants to put his name on everything, and lashes out the way someone does when it’s not clear what’s bigger — their ego or their insecurity.
I’ve been to Nebraska, by the way. Nice place, met a lot of lovely people.
I enjoy corn, on or off the cob.
Popcorn. Caramel corn.
Not wild about “Children of the Corn,” the slasher movie based on Stephen King’s short story. But thank you very much, Nebraska, for Fred Astaire, Johnny Carson and Henry Fonda, who, by the way, was born in Grand Island, where Trump made his cracks Monday about California.
Did it occur to any of the shuckers who cheered Trump’s throwaway line about an attack on San Diego and L.A. that:
A: It wasn’t funny.
B: San Diego has one of the nation’s largest military installations, with thousands of personnel currently deployed to the Middle East because of the war in Iran.
C: Maybe we should expect more from someone serving as president and commander in chief.
In defending Trump, the White House said news outlets had misunderstood and misrepresented the president’s comments in what amounted to a “media freakout.” A White House media post singled out an L.A. Times post that said Trump suggested “letting Iran take out” L.A. and San Diego.
“No, he didn’t, you buffoons,” said the White House. “He was saying the U.S. is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance.”
Please.
This buffoon would like to point out that this is yet another case of Trump using California as a punching bag to prop up support for the war and nail down what’s left of his diminishing base. But even some of his longtime disciples know that he has said on dozens of occasions that the war had ended, was ending, or had been won, and not once were any of those words rooted in reality.
It’s not clear whether we’re any safer in the U.S. as a result of the war, although it is clear that we have paid with lives and higher costs.
So maybe a gratuitous and unfunny line about anyone taking out American cities is better left unsaid.
I’m fresh out of muzzles, but I do have extra poop bags.
steve.lopez@latimes.com

NEW DELHI: Hours before CBI carried out searches at Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann's camp office in Chandigarh and registered an FIR against his OSD and others, Punjab govt had rushed Supreme Court to urgently hear its appeal against Punjab and Haryana HC's Monday order directing the agency to probe ED's allegation that a bribe syndicate influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions through an OSD in the CM's office.Fearing imminent coercive action - based on the HC order for registration of an FIR - by CBI against top politicians and bureaucrats in the state, the Mann-led AAP govt in its appeal sought an urgent stay of the HC's directions. "If the impugned judgement is not stayed, CBI will register an FIR against high public functionaries of the state on untested material... and the situation will become irreversible," it said.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the state govt, said HC had brushed aside the state's preliminary objections, declined three weeks to Punjab Police to complete the preliminary inquiry, which it initiated based on ED's communication levelling "cash-for-transfers postings" allegation, and directed a CBI probe, contrary to the federal scheme of governance mandated by the Constitution."Please hear the petition today itself at 2pm," Singh requested a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.
When the bench said it was impossible to take the appeal for hearing Tuesday itself, Singh said the appeal must be heard Wednesday, suggesting the development can have potentially a huge political fallout in the poll-bound state and arguing that the order marked a breach of the federal scheme of governance.The bench said the state's petition will be listed for hearing either Wednesday or Thursday.In its appeal, the state govt revealed ED's Jalandhar zonal office on July 30 sent a 150-page communication to Punjab DGP under PMLA, alleging it was found that one Nihal Gohal, whose premises were searched in May, influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions "through an officer on special duty in the office of CM".DGP marked the communication, large parts of which were illegible, to Punjab Bureau of Investigation on Aug 3. The bureau began its preliminary inquiry within two days and started collecting evidence from different departments. It sent reminders to ED on Aug 28, Sept 2 and Sept 5, asking it to depute an officer with complete records, but no cooperation was received till Sept 7, the state claimed.
HC had ordered a CBI probe because of what it held to be inaction in the registeration of an FIR on the material evidence sent by ED and had said, "Prima facie allegations with regard to scams including cash for transfers, cash for getting favourable policies, cash for tenders, and such other illegal activities corruption in high public offices have been substantiated by ED with reference to various WhatsApp chats and other information..."Punjab govt said the high court erred by sending CBI into a state which had withdrawn consent to the agency needed to carry out an investigation in the state's jurisdiction, without citing any exceptional circumstances that warranted a CBI probe.In 2010, SC had ruled that SC and HCs can direct a CBI probe in exceptional cases even in states which have withdrawn general consent.

Ukrainian lawmaker Alexey Goncharenko has been expelled from the European Solidarity parliamentary group and added to the notorious Mirotvorets website, which publishes personal information on people it considers “enemies” of the country.
The MP came under fire after publicly calling for peace with Russia and arguing that Kiev is losing the conflict. He suggested that Ukraine should consider concessions to secure a lasting settlement, including abandoning its NATO ambitions, easing sanctions on Russia, strengthening the status of the Russian language, and potentially ceding territory.
The remarks triggered a backlash from politicians and public figures opposed to such concessions, including Vladimir Zelensky, who described Goncharenko’s proposals as an “abnormal message” that undermined national “unity.” The Ukrainian leader nevertheless acknowledged the MP’s right to express his views, citing freedom of speech.
On Monday, Goncharenko was booted from the parliamentary group of the European Solidarity party, led by ex-President Pyotr Poroshenko. The party said the MP’s remarks went against its “ideological foundations” and that proposing any concessions to Russia was unacceptable. On Tuesday, the lawmaker was put on the Mirotvorets hit list over his alleged efforts to “demoralize society,” acting in Russia’s interests, and derailing the mobilization efforts.
The MP has expressed regret over his former party’s decision but stood by his original remarks. He also claimed that he was among the first to speak about the chaotic and violent mobilization drive, while such criticism has now become a commonplace among Ukrainian politicians and public figures.
“I am not saying there are simple solutions. There aren’t. But I am not saying that seeking peace means surrendering. To surrender means to stop looking for ways to end the war,” he said in a statement, calling for “searching for peace together.”
Goncharenko used to be an outspoken Ukrainian warhawk, repeatedly making belligerent remarks against Russia and local Ukrainian Russian-speakers alike. The rhetoric garnered him an official terrorist label in Russia, as well as being sentenced to lengthy prison terms in absentia. Late last year, the lawmaker was found guilty of publicly inciting terrorism and sowing hatred based on nationality and sentenced to 18 years, while in 2024 he received ten years for spreading misinformation about the Russian military, justifying terrorism, and other crimes.
The apparent change of heart by Goncharenko came amid the ongoing retaliatory campaign waged by Russia over the past few weeks, which was prompted by Kiev’s efforts to strike Russia’s energy sector, civilian shipping, and other targets. The result has been heavy damage to Ukraine’s own maritime traffic, dual-use critical infrastructure, and various stockpiles and warehouses used for military needs.

Christa Pike is conscious and speaking at a hospital nearly a week after Tennessee's failed execution, her attorneys say.
In a statement, attorneys for Pike said she remains handcuffed and shackled despite suffering significant injuries to her arms after two lethal injections of pentobarbital failed to kill her.
The statement described her prognosis as unclear.
The US state of Tennessee tried to execute Pike, 50, by lethal injection at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville on the night of September 30.
The IV team struggled for a long time to find a vein — her lawyers say at least seven needles were used, one bent at a right angle when removed — and then administered two full doses of pentobarbital.
She was taken by ambulance to a Nashville hospital with both arms swollen, burned, and blistered, which her lawyers attribute to the caustic drug leaking into tissue after veins blew.
Governor Bill Lee halted executions for the rest of 2026 and ordered an independent review; the prisons commissioner later resigned.
Pike had been on death row since 1996 for the January 12, 1995 torture-murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a classmate at a Knoxville Job Corps centre.
At 18, Pike and her partner, Tadaryl Shipp, lured Slemmer into the woods near the University of Tennessee over jealousy.
They killed her by smashing her skull with a chunk of asphalt.
Pike was arrested within 36 hours and convicted of first-degree murder.
Shipp, 17 at the time, received life.
Pike was the only woman on Tennessee’s death row.
Botched execution divides
The botched execution has rankled people for opposite reasons, and the details of the attempt made both reactions sharper.
The procedure itself looked like a prolonged failure rather than a controlled execution. Staff took a long time to place an IV, using at least seven needles by her lawyers’ account, one of them bent at a right angle when removed.
She stayed conscious, cried and whimpered, and said her arm felt like it was about to burst.
Two full doses of pentobarbital still did not stop her heart.
Her lawyers say the lines were misplaced or the veins blew, so the caustic drug leaked into tissue; she arrived at the hospital with both arms swollen, burned, and blistered, then remained unconscious and on a ventilator.
Others are rankled that the sentence was not carried out at all.

US firm gets $2.9bn sub deal after boss joins war study with Musk
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
21:11:39 UTC
06:11:39 KST

US firm gets $2.9bn sub deal after boss joins war study with Musk
Anduril said it would invest $3.7bn to develop shipyard that would build submarine parts.
Defence technology firm Anduril said it will invest $3.7bn to develop a new shipyard in the US state of Maryland and will build critical components for the United States Navy’s Virginia-class submarines, as Washington seeks to bolster its maritime defence capabilities.
California-based Anduril Industries confirmed on Tuesday it would invest in the submarine production plant, dubbed Arsenal-2, and will receive a $2.9bn US navy contract to manufacture submarine parts.
US President Donald Trump was set to unveil the project and announce a massive naval shipyard expansion in Baltimore, Maryland, on Tuesday afternoon.
Anduril is a defence technology firm whose co-founder, Palmer Luckey, is heading a new Defense Department project alongside technology billionaire and former top Trump adviser Elon Musk. Luckey and Musk were tapped by the Pentagon to lead Project Meridian, a newly-disclosed initiative focused on the future of warfare, including autonomous, AI-powered and maritime military capabilities.
Valued at nearly $117bn, Anduril specialises in uncrewed underwater vehicles and ocean vessels – or naval drones – designed for the US military and its allies.
The initiative was announced at Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s State of the Force address last week in Virginia, part of a 120-day study aimed at identifying new technology needed for next-generation US battlefield supremacy.
The investment is the latest in a series of broader steps by the Pentagon to accelerate naval shipbuilding and weapons production, spurred by the war on Iran and other regional conflicts that continue to threaten global oil traffic while highlighting the critical role of maritime power.
Anduril, founded in 2017 by Luckey, is best known for its military autonomous systems, drones and software.
The startup has, however, expanded beyond drones into maritime and undersea systems, as well as command-and-control software designed to connect military sensors, weapons and other systems.
The Maryland facility will manufacture torpedo tubes and larger hull components for the US navy’s upgraded Virginia-class fast attack submarines, which the navy is renovating to carry up to 40 Tomahawk missiles each.
While nuclear-powered, the warships are not part of the US’s strategic nuclear deterrent system.
The facility is expected to generate 3,100 jobs while supporting over 11,000 indirect roles.
The navy currently operates 26 Virginia-class fast-attack boats, with two more slated for delivery in 2027. According to reports released by the Department of Defense and navy officials, American shipyards have been struggling to meet the Pentagon’s target production rate of two new boats per year due to persistent supply chain disruptions and labour shortages.
Official disclosures confirm the delivery rate has stalled at just 1.1 to 1.2 submarines annually.
Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Anduril President Chris Brose said the “main focus” of the new yard was prioritising component manufacturing for the Virginia-class submarines rather than developing any new drone platforms.
“It’s really the government buying the results of what we’re able to produce from the facility that we’ve invested in,” he said.
