Blood, Bombs & Billions
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
16:12:28 UTC
01:12:28 KST

Blood, Bombs & Billions
For some in America, every new war comes with a new payday.
TEHRAN- The US-Israeli war against Iran was not merely a military and geopolitical crisis; it also created a major economic shock. According to an estimate by the US Congressional Budget Office (CBO), the direct cost of US combat operations against Iran had reached approximately $38 billion by August 1, 2026. That figure includes the cost of replacing expended munitions and lost equipment, increased flight hours, military operations, and higher fuel costs. It does not include costs borne by other federal agencies or the war’s longer-term economic consequences.
At the same time, Americans faced a sharp increase in energy costs. According to an estimate by the Democratic members of the Joint Economic Committee, US households had spent an additional $71.5 billion on gasoline since the war began an average of about $604 per household.
Public opinion also showed that the war did not enjoy broad support. In a June 2026 Quinnipiac poll, 60 percent of American voters said the military action against Iran was not worth the cost, while only 34 percent said it was. A Reuters/Ipsos poll similarly found that just 25 percent of Americans believed the war was worth it, while President Trump’s approval rating had fallen to 34 percent.
Under these circumstances, the important question is not simply whether the war has a cost. The more important question is: Who ultimately pays those costs, and who benefits financially from the consequences of the war? Every dollar spent on missiles, air-defense systems, aircraft, or ammunition creates revenue for a defense contractor. Every sharp increase in oil prices that means higher costs for consumers at the gas pump can translate into higher revenues and asset values for oil producers, refiners, and energy investors. And every surge in financial markets can generate substantial gains for investors who happened to be positioned correctly gains from which the average American has little or no direct benefit.
The broader picture, therefore, is one in which a large part of American society faces higher public spending, more expensive energy, and an unpopular war.
But the war has not been equally costly for everyone. For some companies, executives, investors, and asset owners, it has instead created an opportunity to increase revenues and wealth. The following sections examine some of the most prominent individuals and mechanisms through which financial benefits have emerged from the conflict.
The Defense Industry: Where the Cost of War Becomes a Contract
One of the clearest examples is the American defense industry. During a war, companies that manufacture missiles, air-defense systems, aircraft, radar systems, and ammunition benefit not only from new contracts but also from the government’s need to replenish weapons and equipment consumed during military operations.
RTX, the parent company of Raytheon, for example, reported $24.7 billion in sales in the second quarter of 2026, up 14 percent from the previous year. Adjusted earnings per share increased by 21 percent, while the company’s backlog reached $289 billion, including $119 billion in defense-related orders.
Lockheed Martin reported a similar expansion. In the second quarter of 2026, the company recorded $20.1 billion in sales and $1.8 billion in net income, while its backlog reached a record $230 billion. A significant portion of that backlog is tied to missile-defense systems and other military programs whose importance increases during periods of war.
At the top of these companies are executives such as Chris Calio, CEO of RTX, and Jim Taiclet, CEO of Lockheed Martin. Their compensation structures include not only salaries but also substantial bonuses and equity-based awards. As a result, rising company revenues and stronger long-term performance can have a direct impact on their personal wealth.
Trump, His Sons and His Son-in-Law: Financial Interests Around the War Economy
Among political figures in the US administration, Donald Trump is particularly significant because, unlike many presidents, he continues to hold substantial investments in publicly traded companies.
This is especially important in the energy sector. According to an analysis by the Democratic members of the Joint Economic Committee, Trump held as much as $45.6 million in oil and gas stocks at the end of 2025. As energy stocks surged in 2026, the value of those holdings rose to as much as $61.1 million, representing an increase in market value of up to $15.5 million.
The rise in oil prices and energy stocks associated with the Iran war had a direct positive effect on the value of the president’s personal holdings. Trump also purchased up to $3.6 million more in oil and gas stocks during the first three months of 2026.
The financial connections between the Trump family and industries benefiting from the war, however, do not stop with the president’s own portfolio.
Donald Trump Jr. has become closely involved with 1789 Capital, while Eric Trump has invested in defense and technology companies through American Ventures, the investment arm associated with Dominari Holdings. Their investment portfolios include startups involved in drones, artificial intelligence, space technology, robotics, and military technology precisely the sectors receiving increased attention as the US expands defense spending and develops new military capabilities.
The significance of these investments becomes clearer when looking at the companies in their portfolios. According to reporting by The Washington Post, at least 15 companies connected to investment portfolios associated with Trump’s sons received approximately $3.2 billion in direct federal business, including contracts, investments, and loans, after the Trump administration came to power. Those companies also had roughly $3.1 billion in future contract opportunities.
A separate report from Democratic members of the House Judiciary Committee claimed that after Donald Trump Jr. joined 1789 Capital, assets under management grew from roughly $150 million to more than $3 billion, while its main fund had generated approximately a 200 percent return as of June 30, 2026.
Taken together, however, the investment activity shows that the Trump family has positioned itself financially in several sectors particularly defense technology and energy that have benefited from the economic consequences of the war.
Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, presents another important case. Kushner owns the investment firm Affinity Partners, which invested heavily in Phoenix Financial, one of Israel’s major financial companies.
The connection is important because Phoenix operates within the broader Israeli financial and investment ecosystem, including investments linked to companies involved in sectors connected to Israel’s defense and security economy. As a result, the expansion of Israel’s war economy and the rise in valuations of related assets have had financial implications for Kushner’s investment firm.
The financial benefit was not merely theoretical. In July 2026, Affinity Partners sold roughly one-quarter of its stake in Phoenix Financial for more than $340 million. CNN reported that the investment generated a return of more than five times the initial purchase price. Affinity nevertheless remained Phoenix’s largest shareholder, retaining about 7.4 percent of the company, a stake worth more than $1 billion at the time.
Still, when an investment in a major Israeli financial company generates more than five times its initial return during a period of intense regional conflict, and the investor is able to cash out more than $340 million while retaining a stake worth over $1 billion, Kushner clearly belongs among the individuals who have financially benefited from the wider regional war economy.
The more sensitive issue is that Kushner is not simply an ordinary investor. He is a close member of Trump’s family and played a major role in Middle Eastern diplomacy. That combination political proximity to power alongside major financial exposure to an economy benefiting from regional conflict makes his investment activity particularly relevant to the broader debate over who benefits financially from war.
Oil: The Other Side of the Equation
The war with Iran naturally had a major impact on global energy markets. Iran, the Persian Gulf, and the Strait of Hormuz sit at the center of one of the world’s most important energy corridors. Increased fears of supply disruptions pushed energy prices higher, creating opportunities for some oil producers and refiners.
Executives at major energy companies such as ExxonMobil, Chevron, Cheniere Energy, and ConocoPhillips were therefore operating in an environment where corporate performance was closely tied to energy prices and global demand.
Executives such as Darren Woods of ExxonMobil and Michael Wirth of Chevron own shares in their respective companies in addition to receiving salaries, bonuses, and other forms of compensation. In Wirth’s case, stock transaction records show that he sold shares worth tens of millions of dollars in 2026.
Similarly, Jack Fusco, CEO of Cheniere Energy, and executives at ConocoPhillips receive part of their compensation through shares and equity awards. As the value of their companies rises, those holdings can increase their personal wealth.
But perhaps more important than the personal wealth of individual executives is the enormous amount of money flowing into the energy industry itself.
According to the Financial Times, US independent refiners were expected to generate approximately $32.4 billion in combined profits over the two quarters following the outbreak of the conflict, compared with about $6.8 billion during the same period a year earlier. Companies such as Marathon Petroleum, Valero, and Phillips 66 benefited from wider refining margins and higher fuel prices.
This is where the contrast between consumers and corporations becomes especially visible: higher fuel prices mean higher costs for American households, while the same conditions can generate significantly higher margins for certain energy companies.
Members of Congress and the Stock-Trading Question
Another layer of the story involves members of Congress. Some senators and representatives traded shares of defense and energy companies in 2026, including companies such as Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics, and Chevron.
The significance of these transactions is not necessarily that they prove wrongdoing. Rather, it is that lawmakers responsible for decisions involving foreign policy, defense spending, and government contracts can, in some cases, simultaneously hold financial positions in industries directly affected by those decisions. That overlap has fueled renewed debate over whether members of Congress should face stricter restrictions on individual stock trading.
Alan Armstrong, a Republican senator, purchased Lockheed Martin shares on March 27, 2026, in a transaction valued between $1,001 and $15,000.
Jared Moskowitz, a Democratic representative, made several purchases of General Dynamics shares in March 2026. One transaction on March 23 was estimated at around $8,000.
Dwight Evans, a Democratic representative, sold General Dynamics shares on June 10, 2026, in a transaction valued between $1,001 and $15,000.
Kevin Hern, a Republican representative, also sold Lockheed Martin shares in two transactions on September 2, 2026, each reported in the $15,001-$50,000 range. Using the midpoint of each range gives an estimated total sale value of roughly $65,000.
Anonymous Traders: Profits Whose Owners Remain Unknown
Perhaps the most unusual part of the story concerns the oil market.
A Reuters investigation identified a series of trades in March and April 2026 that bet on falling oil prices shortly before several major Trump announcements concerning Iran. The combined value of these positions was estimated at up to $7 billion. The trades involved futures contracts for crude oil, diesel, and gasoline on major US markets.
The identities of the traders remain unknown. And $7 billion refers to the value of the positions. Nevertheless, the timing of some trades raised questions because they occurred shortly before major political announcements that could have caused significant movements in oil prices.
 
US regulators were reportedly investigating the activity, but there is no public proof that the traders had access to illegal inside information.
A similar pattern appeared on the prediction market Polymarket. Roughly 150 accounts reportedly bet on the likelihood of a US-Israeli attack on Iran shortly before it occurred, with 16 accounts making more than $100,000. One anonymous account known as “Magamyman” reportedly earned around $553,000. A crypto-data analysis also identified six accounts suspected of having potentially used insider information, with combined gains of approximately $1.2 million.
The financial dimension of the Iran war ultimately reveals a striking contradiction at the heart of Trump’s presidency: while American taxpayers and households absorbed the costs of military operations and higher energy prices, Trump himself stood to become wealthier as the value of his oil and gas holdings increased. His family’s investments in defense technology and Jared Kushner’s highly profitable investment in Israel’s financial sector reinforce the same broader pattern: the economic consequences of war do not fall equally on everyone. For Trump in particular, war-driven increases in energy prices and defense spending have created financial opportunities alongside the political and strategic consequences of the conflict.

Rahul Gandhi being detained by police personnel after over eight-hour sit-in inside Akashvani Bhawan premises along with several other MPs.
NEW DELHI: Amid the onging row with opposition parties over SIR, the Election Commission of India on Tuesday said that no political party had formally sought an appointment to meet."Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some Members of Parliament wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to today's developments, it is clarified that, till 4.00 PM today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission," said the EC in a statement.
The EC added that it found out through Delhi Police that "a delegation of MPs, led by the Hon'ble leader of the opposition, Shri Rahul Gandhi, wished to meet the Commission and submit a memorandum."Further clarifying the rules and justifying itself, the EC cited procedures laid down for meetings with political parties. "All political parties had been informed of the same and they follow this procedure. Whenever a delegation of a political party, or a joint delegation of several parties, wishes to meet the Commission, it seeks an appointment through its duly Authorised Representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides," it said.The EC further claimed that after 4 PM, while it was considering the proposed meeting, the Delhi Police informed it that the delegation comprised 240 MPs and that they wanted to meet at the Parliament House Annexe.
The Commission termed the request “unusual” and said it could not be accepted because, under ECI protocol, meetings with political parties are held only at the Commission’s premises.The poll panel said it then offered to send its senior-most officer on duty to the Parliament House Annexe to receive the MPs’ memorandum. The EC described this as “an unprecedented step”, but said the offer was also declined by the MPs.
The Commission said it respected “the parliamentary and democratic processes of the country”, while stressing that its own protocols and conventions were also important. It reiterated that political parties can request meetings with the EC at any time, after which the Commission schedules a date and time depending on its availability.
This came as INDIA bloc leaders staged a massive march from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, demanding a meeting with the poll panel over their allegations of “vote chori” and seeking the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined the sit-in near Akashvani Bhavan, but police later cleared the protest site and detained several opposition MPs.Read more: Rahul and Priyanka removed from protest site after high drama - watch

Ukraine will not agree to permanent restrictions on agricultural exports after joining EU, minister says
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
19:11:00 EEST
01:11:00 KST

Ukraine will not agree to permanent restrictions on agricultural exports after joining EU, minister says
Ukraine "cannot agree" to an EU membership model that would permanently limit sales of certain food products to the bloc.
Source: Taras Vysotskyi, Minister of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine, in a comment to Politico; European Pravda
Details: Vysotskyi made it clear that Ukraine does not approve of a model that would entail agricultural restriction as part of membership conditions solely for Ukraine.
Quote from Vysotskyi: "For us, there is a fundamental difference between a transitional period and a permanent restriction. Ukraine is prepared for the former. The latter would run counter to the very logic of full European Union membership."
The European Commission's proposal, presented on 6 October, states that it wants to "significantly limit financial support and market access for sensitive agricultural products" from Ukraine.
Instead of giving Kyiv full market access, the European Commission would rather help Ukraine get back into its "historic" export markets, which include Africa and the Middle East, the draft document states.
At the same time, Vysotskyi insists that Ukraine should not be seen as a sole threat to European farmers. He argues that Ukraine could help the EU become less dependent on imports from third countries for commodities such as fertilisers, soybeans and lysine for animal feed, and give EU producers better access to export routes via the Black Sea.
Ukraine could also be a place to invest in food processing facilities, Vysotskyi noted.
Quote from Vysotskyi: "Our goal is to reach membership with a sector that sells Europe not only grain and other raw materials but also animal feed, ingredients, processed products, and biofuels."
Vysotskyi confirmed that Ukraine is open to a transition period, which could include phasing in farm support, temporary quotas and safeguards for sensitive products. However, he stressed that such measures must have a clearly defined end date.
Background:
- On 6 October, European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos stated in the context of Ukraine's EU accession that the scale, structure and very high productivity of Ukraine's agricultural sector make it necessary to explore targeted solutions that will only apply to sensitive agricultural products.
- It was previously reported that Kos wants to open two more clusters for Ukraine and Moldova next week.

Sheikh Qassem saluted the dear Iraqi people, their religious authority, leadership, and the Popular Mobilization Forces [Al Hashd Al Shaabi], because “they succeeded in expelling the American occupier from Iraq, and through their sacrifices and steadfastness, they were able to drive the American tyrant out of their country”.

But given the nobility of this people and its sacrifices, it must emerge victorious,” Sheikh Qassem said, “I pray to Allah Almighty to grant them success in occupied Palestine, in Gaza, the West Bank, and Al-Quds, so that they may attain the highest ranks and positions, and that they may be liberated and liberate.”
Speaking on the occasion of the launch ceremony of the Foundation for the Preservation and Dissemination of the Heritage of Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah, Sheikh Qassem said: “Today, we gather under the auspices of the memory of the two noble martyrs, the two esteemed Sayyeds: the Master of the Martyrs of the Ummah, Sayyed Hasan Nasrallah, may God Almighty have mercy upon him, and the Hashemite Sayyed, may God Almighty have mercy upon him, as well as the righteous martyrs, to launch this foundation, which will be dedicated to preserving the works and heritage of the supreme martyr, Sayyed Hassan, may God Almighty have mercy upon him. He continued: “However, from 1992 until his martyrdom—31 years—he worked to consolidate the foundations of the Resistance, the foundations of this authentic thought, and the foundations of an orientation that would govern and influence future generations in pursuit of liberation, dignity, honor, and a virtuous and happy life in obedience to Almighty God.”

We need to collect and archive this material and make it available to researchers and the public through social media platforms, as well as through publications, books, and various works. It should also serve as material for analysis by institutions and researchers at universities and in different fields, so that they may benefit from the abundance of material presented at the intellectual and cultural levels, as well as at the political and practical levels.”
He stressed: “We are dealing with a great treasure that must be collected and made available to the public, researchers, and future generations. This is why the Foundation for the Preservation and Dissemination of the Heritage of the Master of the Martyrs of the Ummah, Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah, may God Almighty have mercy upon him, has been launched.”

Ukrainian chain of stores specializing in semi-finished foods Multi Cook has entered the Serbian market, its founder, Volodymyr Matviychuk, said.
"Serbia is our new country on the Multi Cook map. Today, Multi Cook is much more than just a franchise. It is a global Ukrainian product that has become a true symbol of our country around the world. Our brand enjoys tremendous customer trust and has high recognition thanks to the fact that we have been successfully operating in many countries in Europe and around the world. And every such opening is another testament to the strength of our team and the resilience of our business. Thank you for believing in the brand, for the great results, and for helping us take Ukrainian business far beyond the country's borders," he wrote on Facebook.
The store was opened by a network partner in Belgrade (2Zh Dunavska St.).
Multi Cook is a Ukrainian chain of specialized stores selling frozen semi-finished food products, created by Volodymyr Matviychuk, one of the founders of the Halia Baluvana store chain. It has been developing under a franchise model since 2022.
The Halia Baluvana chain was founded in Lutsk in 2018. Since 2022, its co-owners have focused on international expansion: Matviychuk under the MultiCook brand, and Alla and Oleksandr Telyha under the Wesoła Pani brand. In 2025, Matviychuk announced his withdrawal from the Halia Baluvana trademark and his intention to develop his own brands: Multi Cook, GABAR and MultiBar.
Today, the Multi Cook chain has more than 270 stores in European countries, the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada and elsewhere. Some locations operate as fast-food establishments under the MultiBar brand, combining retail sales with the serving of ready-made meals.

Three years after October 7, is the IDF ready to stop another invasion? - analysis
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
16:06:56 UTC
01:06:56 KST

After days of hearing how incompetent Israel's entire security apparatus is at checking pilot security for foreign airlines, it is necessary to ask, with trepidation: Three years after October 7, is the IDF really ready enough to prevent a potential future invasion?
The answer varies depending on which front we are discussing.
Israel's neighbors include: Lebanon, the West Bank, the Gaza Strip, Syria, Jordan, and Egypt.
The short version is that the chances of an impending large-scale October 7-style invasion are extremely low for the next year, while more unpredictable five years or more down the road.
The IDF is still on the attack and has large security zones in Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza, which it lacked before October 7. In the West Bank, the IDF has 25 battalions, up from 11, and has large contingents of soldiers deep in problem cities such as Jenin, Tulkarm, and Nur al-Shams.
How long the IDF will maintain these security zones remains an open question.
The Trump administration has pressured Israel to undertake at least partial withdrawals from each zone, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has resisted to date, other than in Lebanon, where he has complied but slow-walked the process.
But what if Trump compels Netanyahu or a potential new premier, Gadi Eisenkot, to withdraw from 63% of Gaza to 30% or 15%? What if the same happens over the next year in Lebanon and Syria?
Will Israel remain ready or go to sleep on the job after several years of quiet within the Green Line?
The Jerusalem Post has received briefings throughout the war and recently in order to paint a picture of the country's readiness.
Where has the IDF improved?
IDF's HUMINT Unit 504, collecting other physical intelligence in Gaza
On October 7, the IDF had no human spies in Gaza and was relying almost entirely on cyber or signal intelligence. The IDF's Intelligence Directorate's Human Intelligence (HUMINT) Unit 504 has gone into overdrive in Gaza since then, but also the IDF has nearly complete freedom to use drones to surveil Hamas from the air, as the terror group has lost the capacity to shoot them down.
Some combination of this and other intelligence helped the IDF nab Mu'in al-Arabid on September 2, which led to the killing of three out of Hamas's five brigade commanders in a matter of weeks, with no response from Hamas.
If Israel keeps up even a fraction of this penetration and pressure, it will be in a much better position to block any invasion plans, which currently Hamas could not even contemplate.
IDF Intelligence's 'Red Team' does not save military from some big misses on Iran
A leading failure of IDF intelligence to disregard Hamas invading as a scenario to plan for was the "groupthink" which infected all Israelis.
IDF Intelligence Chief Maj.-Gen. Shlomi Binder, who took over in August 2024, made a wise move in elevating "red teams," whose main job is to play devil's advocate to accepted theories, to having brigade-level human and technological resources, adding hundreds of officers and a more senior commander.
But IDF intelligence has not stopped missing major strategic issues.
During Operation Roaring Lion, IDF intelligence believed it could and had destroyed a much larger quantity of Iran's ballistic missiles and launchers than it actually did (though it did succeed in disrupting future production), which majorly impacted and impacts the broader strategic picture.
Israeli recommendations to the US about whether the Strait of Hormuz would present a major dilemma that could change the course of the war were wildly off.
IDF intelligence has also been overly optimistic about its ongoing pressure on Hezbollah leading to progress in at least partial disarmament. These issues do not relate directly to invasions, but they show large holes still exist in the intelligence establishment due to "groupthink."
This shows that even with "red teams," large institutions use paradigms to map out their work and plan their budgets and rarely second-guess those paradigms.
Technology, Islam experts, and AI
A major failure of October 7 was that IDF intelligence had been reducing the number of Arabic speakers and experts in Islam in recent years.
Hacking and intercepting signal intelligence could be used to rapidly translate Arabic messages for non-Arabic speakers. Since October 7, IDF intelligence has been filling the empty seats of Arabic speakers and experts.
But IDF intelligence is about to embark on a new AI-agent revolution. AI will not only be used to help IDF officers complete tasks faster, but will also start to co-plan and map out basic strategy with them.
The upside is that AI agents are expected to identify new methods to gather intelligence that humans could not arrive at on their own.
But the downside could be that only a couple of years after bringing back the human cultural understanding element, IDF intelligence may once again become more dominated by technology, which could lead to missing complex nuances that only human experts of Islam might catch.
There is no question that, initially, after October 7, the IDF has been taking its mostly female, low-ranking observers more seriously.
Infamously, the female observers who constantly warned of potential Hamas invasion threats had been ignored prior to October 7.
The playing field has changed. The lookouts are now pouring over Hamas moves deep within Gaza near the yellow line where Israel's 63% of Gaza territory meets Hamas's area. This is a big improvement from looking at Hamas on Israel's border.
But some lookouts have complained that, once again, their warnings are not being acted on, even though they are being heard. One lookout recently said that now soldiers on the yellow line can only open fire on Hamas with approvals from top commanders at IDF headquarters as opposed to with approvals from battalion field commanders. If so, she asked, "What is the point of reporting Hamas movements?"
This is not a good dynamic for moving forward.
The question of whether Israel has enough troops on the border is ongoing and dynamic.
IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir said this week that the IDF will coordinate its size and readiness along the borders based on its enemies' capabilities, not on intelligence assessments of their intentions.
This includes the fact that the number of forces assigned to readiness and reserve roles across all sectors has doubled.
That sounds good in principle, and if you ask Zamir, he will say that this also means the standing army policing the borders all around is twice what it was in October
But that is not really the question, as twice as many soldiers would not have stopped Hamas's invasion either, given that Hamas outnumbered Israeli defenders around 10-to-1.
So the better question is: How quickly can the IDF multiply its numbers by three or four times? If it can be done in 30 minutes or two hours, then many of the problems from October 7 could be mitigated.
Once it becomes three hours or more, it might still be too late.
Zamir's speech this week, saying that he has given and will give greater freedom to field commanders to take action and deploy, as well as saying that the IDF is working harder to help headquarters get better and faster understandings of the true situation on the border, might improve reaction time for sending reinforcements. But all of this still depends on the IDF and the country continuing to take Hamas seriously even years into the future.
In addition, the IDF is bragging about its amazing new technologies and connectivity between all sensors. This is fantastic if everything is going well, but if there are no backup sensors that are mobile and that Hamas cannot see, surveil, and plan against, then the Gaza terror group could try to surprise attack the sensors again, the same as it did three years ago.
In May, the IDF assassinated Hamas's military chief, and then assassinated his replacement within a period of weeks. The group could not respond in any meaningful way.
The IDF seems to strike Hamas officials at will on an almost daily basis, even in a period when, nominally, the sides have been in a ceasefire for a year.
Paradoxically, this has led the IDF to now exhibit an even greater superiority complex than it did prior to October 7.
To avoid falling into the overconfidence of dismissing Hamas, IDF intelligence has shifted gears so that its field and technological intelligence arms now conduct separate evaluations of the threat.
In addition, there are now both short- and long-term assessments of the invasion threat, which might help catch threats that were previously missed. In the past, short- and long-term trends were conflated, often leading to the dismissal of potentially distant, dangerous trends in the face of the seemingly endless quiet of the present, which made everyone feel more complacent.
All of this has combined with a still relatively new full brigade of hundreds of officers focused on the warning mission, including a brigadier-general-level commander, to better ensure that warnings are taken seriously throughout the IDF's Byzantine bureaucracy.
Israel currently has most of its enemies on the run.
Yet, politics can get in the way. The government's unforced error of permitting National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir to block police efforts to rein in Jewish extremist violence in the West Bank has made the area Israel's current most dangerous front.
Further, it is human nature to lose focus, and relying on technology has its own dangers.
In fact, avoiding an overreliance on technology may have been a post-October 7 blip on a trajectory in which human intuition continues to be deemphasized, just as most of humanity continues to give up more of its functions to AI automation.
Three years late, "V", the junior female intelligence officer whose personal intuition and warnings about Hamas's invasion plans were ignored by her superiors, received an award. That is the right message, if belated, to send to the IDF intelligence corps.
But with AI ascendant, how many "V"s will be ready to protect Israel in the future?

UK police arrest 7th suspect in connection with alleged air base terror plot
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
16:05:02 UTC
01:05:02 KST

British police on Tuesday arrested a 22-year-old man in London on suspicion of a terror offense over a security incident at a U.S.-run military air base in England that authorities have linked to Iran.
The arrest is the seventh in connection with a suspected plot against RAF Fairford, located 100 miles (160 kilometers) west of London, which has been used by American planes to strike Iran during this year's war.
Police have released few details of their investigation into an incident that sparked speculation and concern — and was followed days later by the removal of U.S. bombers from the base.
Five British men in their 20s were detained near the perimeter of the base in the early hours of Sept. 27, and a 25-year-old British-Iranian man was arrested in London on Thursday. All six have been released on bail under investigation.
Counter Terrorism Policing said a British national was detained Tuesday in the Westminster area of central London on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts.
Vicki Evans, the senior national coordinator for counterterrorism policing, said detectives “remain committed to investigating all possible angles.”
“We’re acutely aware of the public interest in this investigation, and we are working around the clock, and at pace, to identify the motivation behind events in Gloucestershire," she said.
Scores of residents were evacuated from their homes near the base as armed police officers and army bomb-disposal experts swooped on the rural area late at night. Police later said they had found a quantity of an accelerant — gasoline — in three vans linked to the five suspects, but no explosives.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the United Kingdom saw “strong indications” that Iran played a part in the incident, without saying why or what the nature of the suspected plot was.
Iran has denied involvement, but it has previously said it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target.
The U.K.-owned base has been used by American B-1 and B-52 bombers during the ongoing Iran war. The British government allowed the U.S. military to use RAF Fairford for what it called defensive strikes on Iranian missiles and their launch sites following Iranian attacks on U.K. interests and Britain’s allies in the Gulf.
The United States moved its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford on Sunday, and the Pentagon said all American bombers at the facility had been redeployed to their home bases in the U.S.
It's unclear whether the move is connected to the arrests. U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that he didn’t want to tempt “the enemy” by having the bombers there.
“We had a threat, and if we’re going to be threatened, we would just move them, and that sort of alleviates that,” he said in Washington. He said that the people who made the threat “would be linked to Iran,” but he didn’t offer details.
British officials have declined to comment on reports that the bombers were moved because of fears of a drone attack on the base.
The prime minister's spokesman, Tom Wells, said Monday he was "not going to comment on foreign nations’ military operations.” But he insisted that RAF Fairford is safe.
The mysterious incident near the base came at a time of heightened tensions around the threat from hostile states, with British security services saying Russia and Iran have both used proxies to commit crimes on U.K. soil. British officials have said the number of national security cases involving activity by hostile states, including Iran, increased by 50% in the six months to December 2025.
U.K. officials also say proxies linked to Iran have been behind a string of arsons and other attacks in the U.K. and other countries, many of them targeting the Jewish community and intended to sow fear. They have previously warned that Tehran could expand its targets in the U.K. if conflicts in the Middle East continue.

Californians blast Trump remark that Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles, San Diego

Californians blast Trump remark that Iran could ‘take out’ Los Angeles, San Diego
LOS ANGELES, Oct 5 - President Donald Trump suggested to a crowd of his supporters in Nebraska that Iran could "take out" a major US city like Los Angeles or San Diego, drawing a swift rebuke from California's Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans.
Trump, speaking at a political rally in the state's farm belt on Monday, discussed American wartime economic sacrifices and said he was determined to "see a tremendous victory, because it verifies all the things we did."
"And again, remember, with the war, it's just artificial, it's a little bit high, it's a small price to pay," he told the crowd in Grand Island, Nebraska, apparently referring to rising prices of fuel, fertilizer and other products attributed to energy market disruptions from the war.
"It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let 'em take out Los Angeles, let 'em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it's going to be over with very soon," he said.
"It's essentially almost over with," Trump went on. "But it's going to end very soon, and it's going to end one way or the other."
On Tuesday, the White House dismissed criticism of the remark. "The media freakout over President Trump’s comments is not rooted in reality. He was clearly stating U.S. cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn't been stopped," White House Director of Communications Steven Cheung said in a social media post. "America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money."
Trump has shrugged off cost-of-living concerns stemming from the Iran conflict before, and he previously downplayed his concerns about the potential for Iran or its allies to launch an attack on US soil.
EARLY VOTING UNDERWAY IN CALIFORNIA
The comment in rural Nebraska, a state Trump won with more than 55% of the vote in the 2024 presidential election, targeted Democratic-run cities in California, a solidly Democratic state the president often criticizes.
Monday's comments prompted a backlash from California officials.
California Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, denounced the Republican president as "deranged and dangerous."
"After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego," he wrote on X.
Newsom, who has positioned himself as a major political foil to Trump and is seen as a potential 2028 presidential candidate, juxtaposed a video clip of Trump in Nebraska with mention of the president's previous rhetoric to justify deploying US military troops to Los Angeles and other cities to fight crime and enforce immigration.
California's early voting for the November midterm elections started on Monday. The president's Republican Party has hoped to win more races in the state in recent years, including this year's gubernatorial election.
Newsom championed the redrawing of California's congressional map last year to favor Democrats in this year's election after Trump pushed for conservative-led Texas to redraw its map to boost Republicans.
One of the Republicans running in a competitive race in a redrawn California district near San Diego, Jim Desmond, distanced himself from Trump's remarks.
"I vehemently disagree with President Trump’s comments. America must stand up to Iran and defend our interests, but the first responsibility of our Commander in Chief is to protect the American people and our homeland," he wrote on X. Olympian cleared in vandalism case seeks watchdog probes of Trump's Reflecting Pool project
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06

Olympian cleared in vandalism case seeks watchdog probes of Trump's Reflecting Pool project
WASHINGTON, Oct 6 - Lawyers for a former US Olympian accused and then cleared of vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool demanded on Tuesday that two government watchdogs investigate the botched renovation of the Washington landmark by President Donald Trump's administration and the now-dismissed criminal case.
Attorneys for David Hearn, a three-time US Olympic canoeist, urged the US Interior Department's inspector general to examine the flawed installation of an "American flag blue" liner at the bottom of the Reflecting Pool beginning in May. They also asked the US Justice Department's inspector general to investigate the case accusing Hearn of destruction of property, which prosecutors dropped weeks after securing an indictment.
The prosecution of Hearn in July came as Trump blamed alleged vandals for algae blooms and peeling liner in the Reflecting Pool despite evidence that mistakes by a government contractor hired by his administration caused the issues.
The troubled renovation of the pool, which stretches about 2,000 feet (610 meters) along a portion of Washington's National Mall, became a political flashpoint over Trump's efforts to remake Washington's landscape and his use of the criminal justice system against those he views as enemies.
Inspectors general act as independent oversight officials to look into potential abuse, waste and fraud within US government agencies.
In a letter to the watchdog offices submitted on Tuesday, lawyers for Hearn alleged "incompetence and wrongdoing" in both the Justice Department and Interior Department.
"Anything less than a full and fair review would be a betrayal of your mission," the lawyers wrote.
A spokesperson for the Department of the Interior alleged Hearn admitted to officers that he tampered with the pool, referring to a court document. The document includes no such admission, but cites a statement from a National Park Service employee, who told investigators that Hearn tugged at the pool lining.
A spokesperson for the Justice Department inspector general declined to comment. A Justice Department spokesperson said the inspector general's office operates independently "and makes its own decisions about what to review."
Federal prosecutors have said in court documents that they became aware of more pervasive problems with the renovation project only after Hearn had been indicted.
Hearn was charged on July 2 with destroying a piece of the pool liner. The case quickly unraveled after prosecutors said documents from the Interior Department showed the damage was likely caused by a flawed installation by the contractor.
US Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro moved to dismiss the case on July 31, drawing a furious reaction from Trump, who appointed her to the post last year. A federal judge last week barred prosecutors from seeking new charges.
The letter from Hearn's lawyers alleges that prosecutors had evidence of the installation flaws at the time Hearn was charged, but went forward with the prosecution anyway. It further alleges that Pirro improperly sought to question a defense expert who was inspecting the pool during a July 17 site visit.
The lawyers urged the Justice Department's inspector general to examine political pressure from Pirro and Trump to bring vandalism cases.
Trump ordered a refurbishment of the Reflecting Pool in time for July's 250th anniversary celebration of US independence. The pool had to be drained again following July 4 celebrations to repair widespread damage to its liner. REUTERS

Russia Holds Major Nuclear Drill, Simulates Two-Reactor Accident at Beloyarsk Plant
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
16:03:54 UTC
01:03:54 KST

More than 1,000 people gathered for the beginning of a two-day emergency exercise at Russia’s Beloyarsk nuclear power plant on Tuesday, Oct. 6, rehearsing the response to simultaneous accidents at two reactors.
The drill, according to Russian state-owned media Oblastnaya Gazeta, will run through Wednesday at the plant and in the nearby town of Zarechny in the Sverdlovsk region. It is Russia’s annual large-scale nuclear emergency exercise, hosted by a different plan each year.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
The plant’s communications department described it as the largest this year in the Ural Federal District and in the country’s nuclear industry.
“We ask you to remain calm and not interrupt your activities,” Beloyarsk Director Yuri Nosov told Zarechny residents, warning they may hear sirens and loudspeaker announcements, and witness crews in protective gear, alongside military vehicles in the streets.
The scenario stimulates a natural disaster combined with failures of reactor safety systems. During the exercise, the plant’s reactors are expected to keep operating normally.
What the drill involves
The multi-unit accident will be modeled on simulators of the plant’s units 3 and 4. Meanwhile, crews will practice evacuating residents, clearing debris and extinguishing simulated fires, and will set up decontamination points inside Zarechny.
The participants will include specialists from operator Rosenergoatom and state nuclear corporation Rosatom, Defense Ministry radiation, chemical and biological defense troops, police and rescuers, medics from Russia’s Federal Medical-Biological Agency (FMBA), plant staff, and local authorities.
Rubio Calls on Russia to Clarify Suspected Plague Case
Ten foreign observers from Belarus and Kazakhstan will also attend the drill to study Russia’s emergency response.
Russian federal regulations require nuclear plant operators to hold such exercises at least once a year. International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safety standards also call for regular drills, including scenarios with emergencies at several reactors on one site.
According to The Moscow Times, Beloyarsk supplies about 16% of the Sverdlovsk region’s electricity.
Drill comes as Russia’s nuclear rhetoric intensifies toward Europe
The drill coincides with escalating Kremlin nuclear rhetoric toward Europe.
Separately on Tuesday, Lithuania’s parliament voted to remove the constitutional provision banning nuclear weapons: 106 lawmakers in favor, 18 against and six abstaining.
To move forward with the decision, the amendment must win at least 94 of 141 votes again in a final vote, scheduled for Jan. 12, 2027, according to LRT.
Lithuanian Parliament Speaker Juozas Olekas said that the decision would strengthen Lithuania’s resilience and deterrence capabilities, while also removing a legal distinction between Lithuania and other EU and NATO members.
“We are responding to Russia’s aggression,” Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said. “If Russia had not started the war in Ukraine, we probably would not be having the discussions we are having today.”
Currently, Lithuania’s prohibits weapons of mass destruction and foreign military bases to be stationed on Lithuanian territory, according to the Article 137. The proposed amendment would remove that ban.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov earlier said that lifting the ban could further escalate tensions in the region.
“A military base is part of military infrastructure. If someone’s military infrastructure – in fact, that of a major NATO member – is approaching our borders, of course, this can only be viewed as a step toward escalation,” he claimed, according to LRT.
“As for Russia, of course, Russia will have to take all necessary measures to guarantee its security,” Peskov continued.
Dmitry Medvedev, former president and current deputy chairman of the Russian Security Council, also threatened Lithuania by saying the country would “disappear from the map of the world” should it lift its longstanding ban.
He claimed NATO would not invoke Article 5 to defend it, as the move would mean a “global catastrophe.”
Medvedev made the remarks on Friday, Sept. 11, after Russia had already threatened Vilnius earlier that same day.
On Oct. 1, Russian President Vladimir Putin threatened Europe with nuclear weapons in case of a “direct attack” on the exclave of Kaliningrad, wedged between Lithuania and Poland.
His comments came after Russia’s embassy in Belgium accused NATO – which is exclusively a defensive alliance – of an “aggressive policy” without specifying which actions prompted the warning.
The warning marked the latest in a string of threats from senior Russian officials aimed at Ukraine’s Western allies, raising fears that the Kremlin may be searching for a possible justification for a direct attack on the Baltic states.

European Commission explains main condition for gradual EU accession, which will also apply to Ukraine
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
19:02:00 EEST
01:02:00 KST

European Commission explains main condition for gradual EU accession, which will also apply to Ukraine
New approaches to the EU accession process, which will also include the idea of gradual integration, will apply only to countries that demonstrate progress in reforms.
Source: Marta Kos, European Commissioner for Enlargement, following a European Commission meeting in Strasbourg, as reported by a European Pravda correspondent
Details: The European commissioner recalled that member states had previously expressed interest in advancing the approach of gradual integration of candidate countries into the EU.
Quote from Kos: "So we want to be much more ambitious to integrate our candidate countries in selected parts of the union ahead of membership."
She stressed that such gradual integration "is not a substitute for full membership", adding that the new approach should be "the accelerator for the enlargement".
Quote: "It is a bridge between the geopolitical need to stabilise our continent while pursuing merit-based enlargement."
Marta Kos stressed that advancing through gradual integration will require two conditions: the candidate country being integrated into EU policies must demonstrate "progress on reforms", as well as "strategic alignment" with the EU's activities.
Quote: "I would compare this with a car, if the car is not running, it makes no sense if we push them from behind and the motor is not running, and the motor can only run if there is the fuel, and the fuel are the reforms in the country."
Marta Kos named four candidate countries that she expects will fall under the EU's new approach: Montenegro, Albania, Ukraine and Moldova. According to the European Commission, all four are showing progress in reforms.
When asked by a journalist why Serbia is not on the list, despite having made sufficient progress in implementing reforms in the past, Kos explained that the reason is the current lack of progress.
Background:
- Earlier reports indicated that the European Commission is proposing a change to the rules for future EU members.
- The European commissioner is also proposing to agree on exceptions for Ukraine in the EU agricultural sector.

Drone Strikes on Ships Near Bulgaria Draw Global Attention
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
16:02:00 UTC
01:02:00 KST

Bulgaria to Let Shoppers Use Their Own Food Containers
Retailers in Bulgaria will have to let customers buy food using their own boxes and containers from February 12 next year, instead of requiring store-provided packaging
The drone attack on two merchant vessels in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea has drawn widespread international attention, with European media focusing on the strike’s location in the maritime zone of a NATO member and the sinking of one ship whose crew remains unaccounted for.
European news agencies have highlighted the incident as part of growing risks for civilian shipping in the Black Sea. Ukrainian media have linked it to an attack on a vessel off the Romanian coast one day earlier, while Russian outlets have so far reported the facts without claiming responsibility or confirming Russian involvement.
Reuters describes the incident as the first confirmed attack on commercial shipping within Bulgaria’s maritime zone. The agency said the strikes occurred about 112 kilometers from Byala and involved the Togo-flagged ALFA WATAN and the Palau-flagged ABLE. One vessel sank and its crew is missing, Reuters reported.
A maritime source cited by Reuters said preliminary assessments indicated a likely Russian origin, although this has not been officially established. Russia has not commented on the incident.
The Associated Press also stressed that the attacks occurred within Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone. It quoted Prime Minister Rumen Radev as describing the incident as a gross violation of international and maritime law, while noting that the drones’ origin remains undetermined and that Bulgaria has mounted a large-scale rescue operation. The agency also pointed to the economic consequences, including higher insurance costs and disruption to Black Sea shipping.
Euronews reported the attack as part of a series of dangerous incidents involving commercial vessels in the western Black Sea. It noted that the strike near Bulgaria came a day after a cargo ship near Romania was hit, killing two people on board. In both cases, the authorities have not officially identified those responsible.
Italy’s ANSA reported on the two vessels, concentrating on the sinking of one ship and the unknown fate of its crew. It also placed the incident in the broader context of the war and reported that Bulgarian authorities held an emergency meeting afterward.
Spain’s Europa Press reported that a search-and-rescue operation had been launched and likewise said responsibility for the attack had not been established.
Ukrainian media have presented the incident as another threat to civilian shipping in the western Black Sea. Ukrinform reported the strikes on ALFA WATAN and ABLE, saying one vessel sank while the 18-member crew of the other was evacuated. The Ukrainian agency described the incident as the first recorded drone attack on ships inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone.
The Ukrainian outlet European Pravda focused more heavily on Rumen Radev’s statement that the war is expanding geographically. It also recalled the incident off Romania in which a grain-carrying merchant vessel was struck and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky blamed Russia.
The attack off Bulgaria has not been officially attributed to Russia, but its occurrence immediately after another incident involving a civilian vessel has increased concerns over the safety of commercial shipping routes in the Black Sea.
Russian media have also reported the incident, although their coverage has been more restrained on its cause and responsibility. Gazeta.Ru reported that commercial vessels off Bulgaria had been attacked by drones for the first time and highlighted the disappearance of sailors after one ship sank.
Russian news agency Interfax, meanwhile, covered the separate incident off Romania a day earlier, in which two sailors died. Its report said that vessel was outside Romania’s territorial waters but inside the country’s exclusive economic zone.
Neither Russian nor European coverage has so far provided official confirmation of who carried out the attack off Bulgaria, leaving a distinction between confirmed facts and preliminary assessments of its origin.
International media broadly agree on the immediate consequences: two commercial vessels were attacked within Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, one sank, 18 sailors were rescued from the other, and the search for the missing crew of the sunken vessel continues.
Although an exclusive economic zone is distinct from territorial waters, the area is crossed by international trade routes linking Black Sea ports with the rest of Europe. An attack on civilian vessels there therefore affects Bulgaria’s security as well as maritime transport, insurance and the movement of goods across the Black Sea.
Current international coverage centers on two parallel issues: the clear increase in risks to civilian shipping and the unresolved question of who carried out the attacks. Ukrainian media increasingly point to a Russian threat, while European agencies have taken a more cautious position, describing a possible Russian connection as a preliminary assessment. The investigation has yet to establish the perpetrator conclusively.
A suspected coordinated attack by aerial and maritime drones on two commercial vessels inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone was likely carried out using a Russian Geran-4 drone

NEW DELHI: An FIR has been registered against a BJP Booth Level Agent (BLA) for allegedly filing "false" Form-7 applications seeking the deletion of 30 voters from the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR).The case is the first FIR registered in Telangana over allegations of submitting Form-7 applications containing "false" information, news agency PTI reported.The FIR was registered at Chikkadapally Police Station against BJP BLA S Balachander following a complaint by an election official. Police have invoked relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Representation of the People Act."Following a complaint that the BLA submitted forms for deletion of 30 electors, we have registered an FIR. The matter is under investigation," a police official told PTI.Earlier, Telangana Congress leaders had approached Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharshan Reddy, alleging that Balachander, the BJP's BLA in Musheerabad, had submitted Form-7 applications seeking deletion of the names of 30 electors.The Congress alleged that the applications amounted to an attempt to unlawfully remove genuine voters from the electoral rolls and sought legal action against those responsible.
The Telangana Congress also approached Hyderabad Police Commissioner VC Sajjanar, seeking registration of an FIR and an SIT investigation into what it described as a suspected BJP plan to carry out large-scale deletion of genuine voters during the SIR.In its complaint, the Congress alleged that the BJP BLA in the Musheerabad assembly constituency had submitted Form-7 applications seeking deletion of the names of another BJP BLA, Sharfuddin, and members of his family.Form-7 is used by voters to file objections to the proposed inclusion or seek deletion of a name from an existing electoral roll.The BJP has rejected the allegations. Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao said that no BJP BLA had submitted any such Form-7 applications.
Meanwhile, Telangana CEO C Sudharshan Reddy on Monday directed District Election Officers (DEOs) to take action against applicants who knowingly submit false statements or declarations in Form-6, Form-6A, Form-7 and Form-8.In a communication to DEOs, the CEO's office said it had taken note of instances involving bulk Form-7 applications submitted before Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), with allegations that some of these applications were not genuine.

'NAZA' opens in US, reigniting debate over Israel's genocide of besieged Palestinians in Gaza
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
16:00:46 UTC
01:00:46 KST

The opening in US theatres of the documentary "NAZA", in which Israeli occupation forces insiders describe what they say was the reckless killing of civilians during the genocide in Gaza, is likely to reignite the searing debate over Washington's military backing for Israel ahead of congressional elections in November.
Israel's genocide of besieged Palestinians in Gaza has sparked global outrage, as have the billions of dollars in American military support provided by successive US administrations. The genocide has bitterly divided Democrats and some Republicans.
The film received a record 25-minute standing ovation when it debuted at the Venice Film Festival.
The backlash in Israel, which holds its own elections at the end of this month, has been equally fierce.
"NAZA", named after the Hebrew acronym for collateral damage, contends that Israeli troops used sophisticated systems — some operated by artificial intelligence — to attack and target suspected Hamas members, conducting strikes that commanders knew would kill high numbers of civilians.
Israeli occupation forces have "categorically" denied the filmmakers’ findings and threatened to track down the soldiers who spoke out.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is being sought by International Criminal Court over war crimes and crimes against humanity, has labelled the film antisemitic, while a Cabinet minister threatened to strip the directors of their citizenship.
Yuval Abraham, one of the co-directors, voiced fears that he may not be able to return home.
Soldiers describe Israeli atrocities
Abraham and co-director Rachel Szor anticipated that the documentary would prompt controversy. Their previous award-winning production, "No Other Land", documented the plight of Palestinians facing forced displacement in the occupied West Bank, receiving critical acclaim internationally while facing severe hostility from Israeli authorities.
"NAZA" relies on a minimalist approach, avoiding archival air strike footage or conventional talking heads in favour of nocturnal interviews on Tel Aviv rooftops with whistleblowers whose identities remain concealed.
Some sketch out operational diagrams by hand.
One soldier recounts targeting starving civilians en route to food distribution points, whilst another likens automated remote strikes to playing a video game. The production team affirmed that all testimonies were rigorously vetted.
Whistleblowers detail the deployment of AI algorithms to process surveillance data across the enclave to identify targets linked to Hamas, compiling a database containing tens of thousands of individuals.
Another system designates structural and residential targets.
Insiders revealed that these automated mechanisms frequently err; in one instance, clearance was granted to attack a single Hamas member despite an estimated toll of 500 civilian casualties.
Gaza genocide
As usual Israeli military authorities defended their genocidal actions in the Palestinian enclave.
While acknowledging the integration of AI tools, officials claimed targeting decisions remain under the remit of intelligence personnel and field commanders.
Legal authorities, international jurists, and human rights bodies have accused Israel of committing genocide through indiscriminate bombardments, the wholesale destruction of civilian infrastructure, and the weaponisation of humanitarian aid.
According to health officials in Gaza, Israeli genocide have killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, with women and children constituting a majority of the victims. Some 21,000 children were killed by Israel in the genocide.
Analysts say this is an undercount and the actual death toll could reach around 200,000, as Palestinians continue to recover bodies buried under the rubble of homes while Israeli forces occupy approximately 60 percent of Gaza.
Academic findings indicate that Washington has provided in excess of $21.7 billion in military funding to Israel since October 2023.
"Much of what is being described was done with American taxpayer money," Abraham noted. "They would never have been able to carry it out without US diplomatic and military support."
Since 1946, the US has provided over $310 billion in military and economic aid to Israel, adjusted for inflation, according to the American think tank, Council on Foreign Relations.
The International Criminal Court has issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and his former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza.
Israel also faces a genocide case at the International Court of Justice for its war on the enclave.

Narcissism and psychopathy are closely linked in women serving prison sentences
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
16:00:28 UTC
01:00:28 KST

A recent study of incarcerated individuals reveals that grandiose, narcissistic personality traits are closely linked to psychopathic tendencies, partially because people with these traits use manipulative strategies to navigate prison environments. This direct relationship between narcissism and psychopathy is especially pronounced in incarcerated women. The research was published in Psychology, Crime & Law.
The Dark Triad is a psychological framework that groups together three aggressive and self-centered personality traits. These include narcissism, which involves an inflated sense of self-importance; Machiavellianism, characterized by a manipulative and cynical approach to others; and psychopathy, marked by emotional coldness, moral disengagement, and a lack of empathy. In everyday settings, psychologists often view these three traits as related but distinct behavioral patterns.
In a restrictive environment like a prison, these personality features can blend together into active survival tactics. Correctional facilities force constant competition for limited resources and informal privileges. Because overt aggression can attract swift formal or informal sanctions, inmates often rely on covert manipulation to maintain their social standing.
Health researcher Gizell Green of the Max Stern Yezreel Valley College in Israel, along with crisis management and security scholars Alena Lochmannová and Ondřej Kolář of the Police Academy of the Czech Republic, wanted to understand how these traits operate under the constraints of incarceration. The researchers proposed that an innate sense of narcissistic entitlement might not automatically lead to psychopathic behavior. Instead, they hypothesized that an intermediate step of calculated manipulation connects the two. They also wanted to investigate whether this behavioral pathway looked different between men and women in custody.
To test these ideas, the researchers surveyed 344 adults serving time in six different Czech prisons. The group included 205 women and 139 men. Participants filled out a demographic questionnaire and a brief psychological assessment known as the Dirty Dozen. This assessment uses a twelve-item rating scale to measure the presence of the three Dark Triad traits.
To encourage honest answers about antisocial behavior, the researchers used a locked collection box so that prison staff could not match responses to specific individuals. The team then used statistical modeling to map the relationships among the three personality traits. Their models accounted for background factors like age, marital status, and the number of children each participant had, as these demographic details can influence criminal trajectories and baseline personality expressions.
The results showed strong associations among all three dark personality traits in the prison sample. Narcissism was robustly linked to elevated levels of Machiavellian tendencies. Both narcissism and Machiavellianism also directly predicted higher levels of psychopathy.
When analyzing the pathways between these traits, the researchers found that Machiavellianism acts as a psychological bridge. Narcissistic desires for dominance and admiration translate into psychopathic callousness partly through the use of calculating and manipulative strategies. In the context of a prison, where informal hierarchies dictate social standing, manipulation functions as a practical tool to secure resources without exposing personal vulnerability. This repeated strategic behavior can foster the emotional detachment characteristic of psychopathy.
The researchers also looked at whether gender changed these behavioral pathways. Their statistical model did not allow the indirect pathway linking narcissism to psychopathy through manipulation to vary by gender, so it was treated as the same for men and women rather than tested for differences. The direct link between narcissism and psychopathy, however, varied measurably depending on gender. For incarcerated women, the direct association between narcissistic traits and psychopathic traits was almost twice as strong as it was for incarcerated men.
In women’s prisons, a grandiose sense of entitlement is more likely to be paired with severe interpersonal hostility and emotional coldness. Female offenders who display pronounced narcissistic behavior represent a more extreme deviation from traditional gender expectations. The researchers suggest this deviation often reflects a more deeply rooted personality pathology that closely aligns with psychopathy.
These findings offer practical guidance for correctional staff managing risk and rehabilitation. Assessment protocols should avoid treating high scores on Dark Triad tests as a single, undifferentiated warning sign. Recognizing how a person’s pursuit of status translates into exploitative tactics can help staff identify inmates who might resort to coercive behavior. Rehabilitation programs can then focus on addressing these specific manipulative strategies rather than just enforcing general rule compliance.
Because the researchers collected all their data at a single point in time, the study cannot establish a definitive sequence of cause and effect. It remains possible that the prison environment first encourages manipulative behavior, which then brings out dormant narcissistic or psychopathic tendencies. The study also lacked a comparison group of people living outside the prison system. Without this baseline, it is impossible to know if this specific blending of personality traits is unique to the custodial environment.
The psychological survey used in the study is brief and might not capture the full range of behaviors associated with psychopathy. Participants in a prison setting might also adjust their answers to protect their reputations, even with anonymous collection methods. Expanding on these findings will require incorporating longer psychological evaluations and reviewing official behavioral records. Observing how these traits manifest in different international justice systems could help clarify how specific prison cultures shape antagonistic behavior.
The study, “The dark path to psychopathy, Machiavellianism as a mediator of the narcissism–psychopathy link among incarcerated men and women: a moderated mediation analysis,” was authored by Gizell Green, Alena Lochmannová, and Ondřej Kolář.

MINI countryman goes ‘untamed’ with its most rugged setup yet for life off-road
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-06
16:00:26 UTC

MINI countryman goes ‘untamed’ with its most rugged setup yet for life off-road
the countryman gets its most rugged setup yet, with a suspension lift, all-terrain tires, and a hard-shell roof tent.
ready to go off-roading
MINI is giving its largest model a little more room to wander. The new Countryman Untamed Edition takes the familiar crossover and raises it on a 15-millimeter suspension lift, fits it with Pirelli Scorpion All Terrain Plus tires, and adds a set of exterior pieces intended to take some abuse away from paved roads. Depending on market and powertrain, the lift adds up to 19 millimeters of ground clearance. MINI has also recalibrated the steering, anti-lock braking system, while ALL4 all-wheel drive is available across compatible versions.
The changes are modest enough that the Countryman still reads instantly as a MINI, though the car‘s stance feels more confident. Its new 19-inch wheels borrow the blunt construction of traditional steel off-road wheels, with five broad spokes and exposed-looking fastening details. A vertically-patterned grille makes the front end feel taller, and new skid plates extend below the bumpers. Matte black protective films cover parts of the wheel arches and side sills, where scratches and stone chips are more likely to accumulate.
Today, October 6th, 2026, designboom heads to Lake Tahoe to see the Untamed Edition’s unveiling in-person and join the team for a test drive across the rugged landscape of California’s Sierra Nevadas.
untamed edition: A MINI BUILT AROUND WEEKENDS OUTSIDE
The MINI Countryman Untamed Edition even makes sense once the car stops moving. MINI worked with Italian manufacturer Autohome on a hard-shell roof tent that opens with integrated gas struts and includes panoramic openings. The Countryman can support up to 75 kilograms on its roof while driving and up to 300 kilograms while stationary, giving the tent a practical place within the vehicle’s setup instead of treating it as a purely visual accessory. An optional tow hitch brings trailer capacity up to 2,000 kilograms.
A separate collaboration with HELINOX extends the idea beyond the vehicle itself through lightweight camping furniture designed around the edition. There is something pleasantly specific about MINI treating the Countryman as a base camp instead of simply applying tougher-looking trim. The roof tent, increased clearance, and tire package each address a different part of the same use case: reaching a campsite, setting up there, and getting back out again.
FROZEN NOMAD BLUE MAKES ITS MINI DEBUT
Frozen Nomad Blue is MINI’s first matte exterior finish offered in series production, joining Hideaway Grey and glossy Nomad Blue alongside Nanuq White and Midnight Black. The muted surface works especially well with the Countryman’s broad shoulders and squared wheel arches, as it softens reflections across the body and gives its surfaces a heavier appearance. Dark Steel replaces brighter exterior accents across the grille surround and underbody pieces, with a small mountain graphic marking the Untamed Edition on the C-pillar.
Inside, MINI continues the outdoor references through texture instead of turning the cabin into an overt camping theme. Nightshade Blue sports seats combine perforated Vescin with knitted sections inspired by rock formations. The dashboard uses a dark gray and blue woven surface, while the redesigned center console gets elastic retaining straps similar to those found on technical bags. Rubber mats extend the idea down to the floor, where a molded pattern is intended to handle dirt brought inside after a trail or campsite stop.
A SMALL LIFT WITH A bigger PURPOSE
The suspension increase itself is fairly restrained. In the United States and Canada, it will be available across every Untamed Edition variant, while European buyers will find the raised setup exclusively on the electric Countryman models. Approach and breakover angles have been revised, and the all-terrain tires come standard in North America. Those changes push the Countryman farther toward dirt roads and rough access tracks without trying to turn the compact crossover into a dedicated trail vehicle.
Production begins at BMW Group Plant Leipzig in November 2026, with the Untamed Edition scheduled to reach markets in early 2027. Depending on region, the package will be offered across combustion and electric Countryman variants, including the Countryman S ALL4 and SE ALL4. It shows how small changes can accumulate around an iconic car: a little extra height, tougher tires, surfaces designed to take scuffs, and a shelter waiting overhead once the road runs out.

type: crossover / special edition
roof tent manufacturer: Autohome | @autohome_official
production: BMW Group Plant Leipzig, Germany
market launch: early 2027
